research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0008/response.json:168:  "note_markdown": "# Sharp incidence-only losses in bivariate prime-field line\u2013point agreement\n\n## Abstract\n\nFor the affine line-versus-point test on \\(\\mathbb F_p^2\\), I prove two exact incidence obstructions. First, for every prime \\(p\\) and every campaign degree \\(101\\le d<p\\), there is a deterministic legal table with local agreement \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), accepted degree exactly \\(d\\) on every affine line, accepted degree \\(d\\) or \\(d+1\\) at every point, and acceptance supported on all lines. Any fractional family of lines that reaches a fixed fraction \\(\\theta\\) of the accepted points of every target line through *other* accepted lines has total weight \\(\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\), with a multiplicative gap at most \\((d+1)/(d-1)\\). Thus the \\(p/\\epsilon\\) scale cannot be improved by a universal graph-theoretic cover, even with exact near-regularity and fractional weights.\n\nSecond, for every table of agreement \\(\\epsilon\\), the probability that two uniformly chosen distinct lines through a uniform point are both accepted there is exactly\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon^2-\\frac{\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)}p+\n\\frac{\\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)},\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(a_x\\) is the accepted degree of \\(x\\). The lower bound is attained by accepting exactly \\(k\\) direction classes. Hence the usual \\(\\epsilon^2\\) collision loss is sharp.\n\nBoth extremal tables have the obvious global polynomial \\(Q=0\\). They are therefore obstructions to incidence-blind proof architectures, not counterexamples to soundness. An exact primary-source audit also shows that KTZ already uses the affine Vinh estimate, while the stronger Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw bounds do not give the linear component size needed for global agreement in their characteristic ranges. The unconditional benchmark exponent remains \\(1/3\\).\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix a prime \\(p\\), an integer \\(101\\le d<p\\), and dimension \\(m=2\\). Let \\(\\mathcal L\\) be the \\(p(p+1)\\) affine lines of \\(\\mathbb F_p^2\\). Every line has \\(p\\) points and every point lies on \\(p+1\\) lines.\n\nA point table is \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\). Each \\(L\\in\\mathcal L\\) has one polynomial label \\(P_L\\) of degree at most \\(d\\), interpreted using a fixed affine parameterization of \\(L\\). Put\n\n\\[\nA(x,L)=1_{\\{P_L(x)=f(x)\\}},\\qquad\n\\epsilon=\\frac{\\sum_{x,L\\ni x}A(x,L)}{p^2(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nThis is exactly uniform-line-then-uniform-point sampling. Let\n\n\\[\na_x=\\sum_{L\\ni x}A(x,L),\\qquad\nN_E(L)=\\{x\\in L:A(x,L)=1\\}.\n\\]\n\nFor nonnegative line weights \\(\\lambda=(\\lambda_M)_{M\\in\\mathcal L}\\), define the capped load reaching an accepted incidence \\((x,L)\\) through other lines by\n\n\\[\nu_{x,L}(\\lambda)=\n\\min\\left\\{1,\\sum_{\\substack{M\\ni x,\\,M\\ne L}}A(x,M)\\lambda_M\\right\\}.\n\\]\n\nFor \\(0<\\theta\\le1\\), call \\(\\lambda\\) \\(\\theta\\)-reaching if\n\n\\[\n\\sum_{x\\in N_E(L)}u_{x,L}(\\lambda)\\ge\\theta |N_E(L)|\n\\quad\\text{for every }L\\in\\mathcal L.\n\\]\n\nIndicator weights are ordinary selected-line families. Fractional weights also cover multisets after coincident copies are combined.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe active corpus contains four earlier submissions and four verifier audits. Researcher-0002 is the only accepted result: a connected accepted component of minimum degree \\(k\\) and line measure \\(\\tau\\) is decoded under \\(k^2\\ge2^{40}dp\\) and \\(k^3\\ge2^{40}d\\tau p^2\\), giving a conditional exponent \\(1/2\\) when \\(\\tau=O(\\epsilon)\\). Researcher-0001 is revise-grade: its support-sensitive cubic theorem and modal obstruction were validated, but its exact statement and mixing algebra need repairs. Researcher-0003 was rejected because its hashed theorem omitted essential hypotheses forcing a \\(Z\\)-dependent interpolant; its weighted-resultant lemma survives only with the fuller hypotheses in the note. Researcher-0004's exact jet count is revise-grade and shows only that uniform rank-blind multiplicity is exponent-neutral. No active submission proves an unconditional exponent above \\(1/3\\). The data manifest is a launch snapshot and is not current mathematical evidence; the live boards and audits control this synthesis.\n\nThe benchmark is [Kominers\u2013Thaler\u2013Zheng, Revision 1, Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, agreement \\(\\epsilon\\ge C(d/q)^{1/3}\\) yields one total-degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomial with global agreement \\(c\\epsilon\\). In its bivariate proof, Lemmas 6.2\u20136.3 give \\(\\epsilon/8000\\). The following explanation is a reconstruction, not a quoted theorem: Lemma 3.2 gives \\(|R|\\le6400p/\\epsilon\\); Section 4 uses \\(D=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{d|R|}\\rfloor+1)\\); and Lemmas 4.1, 4.3, and 6.1 require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\). Hence \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\). KTZ supplies one-sided bounds, not simultaneous \\(\\Theta\\)-saturation.\n\nThe exact affine spectral estimate already appears as KTZ Lemma 2.1. Its primary antecedent is [Vinh, Theorem 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0711.4427v1):\n\n\\[\nI(P,T)\\le\\frac{|P||T|}{p}+\\sqrt{p|P||T|}.\n\\]\n\nFor medium-size distinct sets, [Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw, Theorem 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.06284v4) proves\n\n\\[\nI(P,T)\\ll |P|^{11/15}|T|^{11/15}\n\\]\n\nonly when \\(|P|^{7/8}<|T|<|P|^{8/7}\\) and \\(|P|^{-2}|T|^{13}\\ll p^{15}\\). Their Theorem 4 additionally treats a genuine Cartesian set \\(A\\times B\\), under \\(|A|\\le|B|\\), \\(|A||B|^2\\le|T|^3\\), and \\(|A||T|\\ll p^2\\). These hypotheses cannot be silently imposed on accepted-point supports. Bourgain\u2013Katz\u2013Tao Theorem 6.2 has an unspecified gain depending on a fixed support exponent and is not used.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A (regular carrier and other-line fractional-cover obstruction).** Let \\(p\\) be prime and let \\(101\\le d<p\\). There exist \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and degree-exactly-\\(d\\) labels \\(P_L\\), one for every affine line, such that:\n\n1. \\(|N_E(L)|=d\\) for every \\(L\\), while \\(a_x\\in\\{d,d+1\\}\\) for every \\(x\\). Exactly \\(pd\\) points have degree \\(d+1\\), and the remaining \\(p(p-d)\\) points have degree \\(d\\).\n2. The agreement is \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), and every affine line supports acceptance.\n3. For every \\(0<\\theta\\le1\\), if \\(\\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta\\) denotes the infimum of \\(\\sum_L\\lambda_L\\) over all nonnegative \\(\\theta\\)-reaching weights, then\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d+1}\n\\le \\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta\n\\le \\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d-1}.\n\\]\n\n4. The total-degree-zero polynomial \\(Q=0\\) satisfies \\(Q(x)=f(x)\\) for every point.\n\n**Lemma B (exact two-line collision identity).** For any valid table in the same ambient regime, let \\(\\Gamma_2\\) be the probability that, after choosing \\(x\\) uniformly and an ordered pair \\((L,M)\\) of distinct lines through \\(x\\) uniformly, both \\((x,L)\\) and \\((x,M)\\) accept. Then\n\n\\[\n\\Gamma_2=\n\\epsilon^2-\\frac{\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)}p+\n\\frac{\\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nFor every integer \\(1\\le k\\le p+1\\), equality in the lower bound is attained by a valid table of ambient degree cap \\(d\\) with \\(\\epsilon=k/(p+1)\\).\n\n**Proposition C (black-box incidence range).** Let a balanced accepted component have \\(N\\) point vertices, \\(N\\) distinct line vertices, and minimum degree at least \\(k\\). If Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw Theorem 3 applies, then \\(N\\gg k^{15/7}\\). This consequence alone reaches \\(N=\\Omega(kp)\\) only outside that theorem's positive-characteristic range. If the point set is additionally a balanced Cartesian product and Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw Theorem 4 applies, its consequence \\(N\\gg k^{8/3}\\) likewise reaches \\(N=\\Omega(kp)\\) only outside its characteristic range.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved: affine incidence decomposition).** Add \\(p\\) dummy point vertices. For each \\(b\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), connect dummy vertex \\(z_b\\) to the \\(p\\) lines \\(y=mx+b\\), \\(m\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), and to the vertical line \\(x=b\\). The resulting bipartite graph has \\(p(p+1)\\) vertices on each side and is \\((p+1)\\)-regular. A regular bipartite graph has a perfect matching: for every left set \\(S\\), its \\((p+1)|S|\\) edges enter at most \\((p+1)|N(S)|\\) slots, so Hall's condition holds. Removing a perfect matching preserves regularity. Iteration decomposes the augmented graph into \\(p+1\\) perfect matchings, regarded as colors.\n\nAfter deleting the dummy edges, every real point sees every color exactly once. Every affine line misses exactly the color of its unique dummy edge. Each color is absent from exactly \\(p\\) affine lines because its perfect matching contains exactly one edge at each of the \\(p\\) dummy vertices.\n\n**[P2] (proved: select and repair colors).** Select any \\(d\\) colors and let \\(E_0\\) be their real incidence edges. Every point has \\(E_0\\)-degree \\(d\\). A line has degree \\(d\\) unless its missing color was selected, in which case it has degree \\(d-1\\). There are exactly \\(pd\\) distinct deficient lines.\n\nPut \\(r=p+1-d>0\\). In the graph of unselected real incidences from deficient lines to real points, every deficient line has degree \\(r\\), while every point has degree at most \\(r\\). Hence for every deficient-line set \\(S\\),\n\n\\[\nr|S|=e(S,N(S))\\le r|N(S)|.\n\\]\n\nHall gives a matching saturating all deficient lines. Add these matching edges to \\(E_0\\). Every line now has degree \\(d\\); the \\(pd\\) distinct matching endpoints have point degree \\(d+1\\), and all other points retain degree \\(d\\).\n\n**[P3] (proved: realize the accepted graph).** Set \\(f=0\\). For each fixed parameterization \\(L(t)\\), let \\(S_L\\subseteq\\mathbb F_p\\) be the \\(d\\) parameters of the selected edges on \\(L\\), and define\n\n\\[\np_L(t)=\\prod_{a\\in S_L}(t-a).\n\\]\n\nThis polynomial has degree exactly \\(d<p\\) and vanishes exactly on \\(S_L\\). Therefore the accepted-incidence graph is precisely the graph from [P2]. Since it has \\(p(p+1)d\\) edges out of \\(p^2(p+1)\\),\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon=d/p.\n\\]\n\nAll lines support acceptance. The legal global polynomial \\(Q=0\\) agrees with \\(f\\) everywhere.\n\n**[P4] (proved: fractional-cover lower bound).** Let \\(\\lambda\\) be \\(\\theta\\)-reaching and define the larger common capped load\n\n\\[\nv_x=\\min\\left\\{1,\\sum_{M\\ni x}A(x,M)\\lambda_M\\right\\}.\n\\]\n\nSince \\(u_{x,L}\\le v_x\\), double counting gives\n\n\\[\n\\theta d\\,p(p+1)\n\\le \\sum_L\\sum_{x\\in N_E(L)}u_{x,L}\n\\le \\sum_x a_xv_x\n\\le(d+1)\\sum_xv_x.\n\\]\n\nAlso\n\n\\[\n\\sum_xv_x\n\\le\\sum_x\\sum_{M\\ni x}A(x,M)\\lambda_M\n=d\\sum_M\\lambda_M.\n\\]\n\nThus\n\n\\[\n\\sum_M\\lambda_M\\ge\\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d+1}.\n\\]\n\nNo Markov, union, or Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss occurs. An ordinary selected set is the special case \\(\\lambda_M\\in\\{0,1\\}\\), so the same lower bound applies to KTZ's stricter other-line reach condition.\n\n**[P5] (proved: fractional-cover upper bound).** Give every line weight \\(\\lambda_M=\\theta/(d-1)\\). At an accepted incidence \\((x,L)\\), at least \\(a_x-1\\ge d-1\\) other accepted lines pass through \\(x\\). Hence \\(u_{x,L}\\ge\\theta\\), so the weights are \\(\\theta\\)-reaching. Their total weight is \\(\\theta p(p+1)/(d-1)\\). This proves Theorem A, including a multiplicative upper-to-lower gap \\((d+1)/(d-1)\\le102/100\\).\n\n**[P6] (proved: collision identity).** For a fixed point \\(x\\), exactly \\(a_x(a_x-1)\\) ordered pairs of distinct incident lines are jointly accepted. Therefore\n\n\\[\n\\Gamma_2=\n\\frac{\\mathbb E_x[a_x(a_x-1)]}{p(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nBecause \\(\\mathbb E_xa_x=(p+1)\\epsilon\\), expanding the variance gives\n\n\\[\n\\Gamma_2=\n\\frac{(p+1)^2\\epsilon^2-(p+1)\\epsilon+\\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)},\n\\]\n\nwhich is Lemma B. In particular, \\(\\Gamma_2\\ge\\epsilon^2-\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)/p\\), and if \\(\\epsilon\\ge2/p\\), then \\(\\Gamma_2\\ge\\epsilon^2/2\\). This is one exact Jensen/variance loss and no further concentration loss.\n\n**[P7] (proved: collision equality and concentrated directions).** Fix \\(k\\) projective directions. Put \\(f=0\\), label every line in those directions by the zero polynomial, and every other line by the constant-one polynomial. These are legal labels under the ambient cap \\(d>100\\). Every point has accepted degree exactly \\(k\\), so the variance term vanishes. The agreement and collision probability are\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon=\\frac{k}{p+1},\\qquad\n\\Gamma_2=\\frac{k(k-1)}{p(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nDirect substitution shows equality in Lemma B. The same \\(Q=0\\) has global agreement one, so concentrated directions sharpen the incidence loss but do not obstruct soundness.\n\n**[P8] (proved: where the KTZ cubic occurs).** KTZ Lemma 3.2 uses sampling rate \\(\\Theta(1/(\\epsilon p))\\), Chernoff plus a union bound over at most \\(p(p+1)\\) target lines, and Chebyshev for sample size. These estimates cost constants and produce only the one-sided upper bound \\(|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)\\). Weighted interpolation then gives\n\n\\[\nD=O\\left(\\sqrt{d|R|}\\right)\n =O\\left(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon}\\right).\n\\]\n\nThe distinct-root and lifting budgets require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\). Squaring gives \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\). Theorem A shows that replacing the cover by a universally \\(o(p/\\epsilon)\\)-weight fractional cover is false, but does not rule out decoding the obstructing case before interpolation.\n\n**[P9] (proved: Vinh/KTZ mixing barrier).** KTZ Lemma 2.1 is the absolute affine form of Vinh's spectral estimate, with normalized error \\((p+1)^{-1/2}\\). Lemma 6.2 absorbs it using\n\n\\[\n(p+1)^{-1/2}\\le\\epsilon/8000.\n\\]\n\nAt the current cubic threshold this is weaker: \\((d/p)^{1/3}\\sqrt p=d^{1/3}p^{1/6}\\). For a prospective exponent \\(\\alpha>1/2\\), however, fix the legal lower boundary \\(d=101\\). If \\(\\epsilon=C(101/p)^\\alpha\\), then\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\sqrt p=C\\,101^\\alpha p^{1/2-\\alpha}\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\n\nThus Vinh-only component recovery cannot establish linear global agreement in this regime. This is a method obstruction, not a counterexample to a stronger theorem.\n\n**[P10] (proved: Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw diagnostics).** In the balanced setting of Proposition C, minimum degree gives \\(kN\\le I(P,T)\\). Theorem 3 gives\n\n\\[\nkN\\ll N^{22/15},\\qquad N\\gg k^{15/7}.\n\\]\n\nFor this lower bound to be at least the required \\(kp\\), one needs \\(k^{8/7}\\gtrsim p\\), or \\(k\\gtrsim p^{7/8}\\). At that scale it forces \\(N\\gtrsim p^{15/8}\\), whereas the theorem's characteristic hypothesis in the balanced case is \\(N^{11}\\ll p^{15}\\), i.e. \\(N\\ll p^{15/11}\\). There is no asymptotic overlap.\n\nIf the balanced point set is genuinely Cartesian, Theorem 4 gives\n\n\\[\nkN\\ll N^{11/8}+N,\n\\qquad N\\gg k^{8/3}\n\\]\n\nonce the linear term is absorbed. Reaching \\(N\\gtrsim kp\\) would require \\(k\\gtrsim p^{3/5}\\) and hence \\(N\\gtrsim p^{8/5}\\). But the characteristic condition \\(|A||T|\\ll p^2\\), with \\(|A|=\\sqrt N\\) and \\(|T|=N\\), requires \\(N\\ll p^{4/3}\\). Again there is no overlap. These are exponent reconstructions from the quoted theorems, not source-stated low-degree-test conclusions.\n\n**[P11] (refuted: incidence-only shortcut).** The claim that acceptance density alone always yields either \\(\\omega(\\epsilon^2)\\) compatible line-pair density or an \\(o(p/\\epsilon)\\)-weight family reaching a fixed fraction of every accepted line is false. Lemma B refutes the first alternative and Theorem A refutes the second. Since both examples have a perfect decoder, they instead prove that a successful argument must branch on algebraic or value coherence.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| KTZ selection | \\(\\epsilon\\) | one inverse \\(\\epsilon\\) | \\(|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)\\) |\n| KTZ interpolation | \\(|R|\\) | square root | \\(D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\) |\n| KTZ root budget | \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\) | cubic comparison | \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\) |\n| Regular construction | degree \\(d\\) | none | \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), line degree \\(d\\), point degree \\(d\\) or \\(d+1\\) |\n| Fractional reach | fraction \\(\\theta\\) | factor between \\(d-1\\) and \\(d+1\\) only | \\(\\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta=\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\) |\n| Collision extraction | \\(\\epsilon\\) | exact square plus finite correction | \\(\\Gamma_2\\ge\\epsilon^2-\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)/p\\) |\n| KTZ/Vinh mixing | component degree \\(\\Theta(\\epsilon p)\\) | \\(p^{-1/2}\\) error | linear recovery only when \\(\\epsilon\\gtrsim p^{-1/2}\\) by this route |\n| Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw, balanced | minimum degree \\(k\\) | exponent \\(15/7\\) | \\(N\\gg k^{15/7}\\), insufficient for \\(N\\gg kp\\) in range |\n| Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw, Cartesian | minimum degree \\(k\\) | exponent \\(8/3\\) | \\(N\\gg k^{8/3}\\), insufficient for \\(N\\gg kp\\) in range |\n| Constructed global output | \\(f=0\\) | none | one \\(Q=0\\) with agreement \\(1\\) |\n\nThe new construction is deterministic. The only convexity loss is exposed exactly by the variance term in Lemma B. No logarithmic, Markov, union, derivative, or multiplicity loss is suppressed.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\nTheorem A is a successful counterexample to a universal smaller reaching family. Unlike the earlier random balanced-color example, it is deterministic, exactly regular on the line side, within one on the point side, supported on every line, valid at \\(d=101\\), and valid near \\(p\\). Its fractional formulation also prevents an apparent escape through line multiplicities or randomized weights.\n\nIt fails completely as a soundness counterexample: \\(f=Q=0\\) everywhere. This is the intended sparsify-or-decode separation. The earlier verifier-accepted balanced-color construction behaves similarly at larger local agreements.\n\nThe direction-class table attains the collision lower bound and tests concentrated good directions. It too has perfect global agreement. Thus neither high collision energy nor direction concentration alone identifies a hard instance.\n\nThe modal table from researcher-0001 remains the only active genuine endpoint obstruction: at ambient \\(d=101\\), it has local agreement \\(\\Theta(\\log p/(p\\log\\log p))\\) and global degree-101 agreement below \\(2/p\\). It refutes a literal constant-times-\\(d/p\\) theorem but stays below every fixed \\((d/p)^{1-\\eta}\\) trigger.\n\nInseparability does not enter either new construction. At \\(d=p-1\\), the regular construction remains valid, but its perfect global polynomial confirms that the near-\\(p\\) regime is not an obstruction.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The ambient field is exactly \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), and \\(101\\le d<p\\).\n- Each root polynomial has \\(d\\) distinct linear factors and formal degree below \\(p\\). Its zero set has exactly \\(d\\) points.\n- No derivative is divided by. The roots are simple, but simplicity is not used.\n- No discriminant, resultant, factor irreducibility, absolute irreducibility, or interpolation multiplicity is invoked.\n- Hall matching is proved directly by degree counting. No probabilistic method or finite computation proves existence.\n- Fixed affine parameterizations avoid division by a slope and treat vertical lines identically.\n- Lines are distinct geometric affine lines. Fractional weights are handled explicitly; source incidence theorems are not silently extended to multisets.\n- Constant labels in [P7] are legal under the fixed ambient cap \\(d>100\\); the excluded test parameter \\(d=0\\) is never studied.\n- At the lower boundary \\(p=103,d=101\\), the complement degree is three. At \\(d=p-1\\), it is two.\n- Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw's positive-characteristic inequalities are retained in [P10]; their implicit constants are not converted into an unstated explicit finite range.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe benchmark is not improved. Theorem A lives at the exact interpolation floor \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), which is below every fixed-\\(\\eta\\) trigger when \\(d/p\\to0\\). It obstructs a proof module, not the target theorem.\n\nConnectivity of the regular accepted graph is not proved. The cover lower bound is global and remains valid regardless of its component decomposition. An algebra-aware algorithm may decode components separately, as \\(Q=0\\) demonstrates.\n\nLemma B controls only pair extraction from acceptance density. Additional polynomial information might distinguish its equality examples. Proposition C audits black-box unweighted incidence estimates only; it does not rule out a new weighted, lifted, or algebra-sensitive incidence theorem.\n\nThe Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw calculations assume balanced components, and the Cartesian calculation additionally assumes a true product set. General accepted components need not satisfy either shape hypothesis. Bourgain\u2013Katz\u2013Tao's fixed-support exponent is insufficiently explicit for the campaign's uniform \\(d,p\\) target and was not imported.\n\nAccordingly, improvement from exponent \\(1/3\\) toward \\(1/2\\) still requires a sparsify-or-decode or interpolation advance. research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0001/response.json:217:  "note_markdown": "# The bivariate prime-field cubic bottleneck: support sensitivity and a modal obstruction\n\n## Abstract\n\nFor the affine line-versus-point test on `F_p\u00b2`, the KTZ cubic threshold comes from one precise chain:\n\n`|R| = O(p/\u03b5)`, `D = \u0398(sqrt(d|R|))`, and `D = O(\u03b5p)`.\n\nThe first relation is the selected-line cost, the second is weighted interpolation, and the third is simultaneously required for identity extension, deletion of nonsimple incidences, and root lifting. Their combination is `\u03b5\u00b3 = \u03a9(d/p)`.\n\nRetaining the fraction \u03c3 of lines supporting an accepted carrier of edge mass \u03b4 gives the sharper proved relation `\u03b4\u00b3 = \u03a9(d\u03c3/p)`. In particular, \u03c3=O(\u03b4) gives a conditional exponent `1/2`, but not an unconditional benchmark improvement. In the prime regime, I also prove that the primitive squarefree interpolant satisfies `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`, so KTZ's generic directional derivative can be replaced by the vertical derivative.\n\nFinally, I give a legal obstruction at ambient degree `d=101`: modal constant line labels can attain local agreement `\u0398(log p/(p log log p))` while every total-degree-at-most-101 polynomial has agreement below `2/p`. Thus a uniform exact threshold `C d/p` with global agreement `\u03a9(\u03b5)` is false. This obstruction remains below every fixed-\u03b7 trigger `(d/p)^(1\u2212\u03b7)`.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix a prime `p` and an integer `101\u2264d<p`; the dimension is exactly two. Let `L` range uniformly over the `p(p+1)` affine lines of `F_p\u00b2`, and then let `x` range uniformly over the `p` points of `L`. This is uniform sampling from the `p\u00b2(p+1)` incidences and is equivalent to first choosing `x` uniformly and then an incident line uniformly.\n\nThe point table is an arbitrary function `f:F_p\u00b2\u2192F_p`. Each line has a univariate polynomial label `P_L` of degree at most `d`. All global degrees below are total degrees. Define\n\n`\u03b5 = Pr_{L,x\u2208L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]`\n\nand\n\n`Agr_d(f) = max_{Q: total-degree(Q)\u2264d} Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]`.\n\nAn accepted carrier is any set `E*` of accepted incidences. Write\n\n`\u03b4 = |E*|/[p\u00b2(p+1)]`,  `T = projection of E* to lines`,  `\u03c3 = |T|/[p(p+1)]`.\n\nNecessarily `0<\u03b4\u2264\u03c3\u22641`. Taking all accepted incidences gives `\u03b4=\u03b5`; a carrier with `\u03b4\u2265\u03b5/2` retains a constant fraction of the test acceptance.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe primary benchmark is [Kominers\u2013Thaler\u2013Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/). Its Theorem 1.1, specialized to the present regime, states that absolute constants `C,c>0` give global agreement at least `c\u03b5` when `\u03b5\u2265C(d/p)^(1/3)`. The theorem statement hides the constants. The bivariate proof in Sections 3\u20136 explicitly closes with recovery `\u03b5/8000`.\n\nThe source chooses `k0=floor(\u03b5p/100)`, `k1=floor(\u03b5p/1000)`, a selected line set of size `O(p/\u03b5)`, and\n\n`D = 16(floor(sqrt(d|R|))+1)`.\n\nRevision 1 uses a squarefree primitive polynomial, a generic directional derivative, and a resultant; it does not use a discriminant in the bivariate proof. The constant `10^15` below is my conservative reconstruction for a support-sensitive variant, not a constant quoted from Theorem 1.1. The older cached base report and Revision 1 must not be conflated.\n\nThe Newton step is consistent with [Harsha\u2013Kumar\u2013Saptharishi\u2013Sudan, arXiv:2311.12752v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12752), especially Lemma 2.10, but the needed lifting argument is reproduced below. No Arora\u2013Sudan theorem is used as a black box.\n\nThe active durable corpus was also audited. All eight active leaderboard files were empty, and there were no completed submissions or verifier-audit files to inherit. The [data manifest](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json) is a pre-launch snapshot relative to the live campaign state, so it was treated as provenance rather than mathematical evidence. Every directory named `superseded` was excluded.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A \u2014 support-sensitive KTZ closure.** Let `p` be prime, `101\u2264d<p`, and let an accepted carrier have parameters `(\u03b4,\u03c3)`. Put `K=10^15`. If\n\n`\u03b4\u00b3 \u2265 K d\u03c3/p`,\n\nthen there is a polynomial `Q\u2208F_p[X,Y]` of total degree at most `d` with\n\n`Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)] \u2265 \u03b4/8000`.\n\nThus, if `\u03b4\u2265\u03b5/2`, the conclusion is at least `\u03b5/16000`. With all accepted edges and \u03c3\u22641, the sufficient threshold is `\u03b5\u226510^5(d/p)^(1/3)`. Under the additional structural condition `\u03c3\u2264A\u03b4`, it becomes the conditional square-root threshold `\u03b4\u2265sqrt(10^15 A d/p)`.\n\n**Lemma B \u2014 prime vertical derivative.** If `B\u2208F_p[X,Y,Z]` is squarefree, primitive as a polynomial in `Z`, and has total degree below `p`, then `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`.\n\n**Theorem C \u2014 modal obstruction at the legal lower boundary.** Let `d=101`, `N=(d+1)(d+2)/2=5253`, and\n\n`r=floor(log p/(4 log log p))`.\n\nFor every sufficiently large prime, explicitly every prime `p\u2265max{\u2308e^32\u2309,100N\u00b2}`, there are a point table and constant line labels, hence labels of degree at most 101, such that\n\n`r/(130p) \u2264 \u03b5 \u2264 50r/p`,  while  `Agr_101(f)<2/p`.\n\nConsequently, for every fixed `C,c>0`, arbitrarily large primes admit `\u03b5\u2265C\u00b7101/p` but `Agr_101(f)<c\u03b5`.\n\n**Proposition D \u2014 near-p information baseline.** For every `101\u2264d<p` and every point table,\n\n`Agr_d(f) \u2265 (d+1)(d+2)/(2p\u00b2)`.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved) Carrier pruning.** Set `k0=floor(\u03b4p/100)`. Iteratively delete point vertices and line vertices whose current carrier degree is below `k0`. Point deletions remove at most `p\u00b2k0` edges and line deletions at most `p(p+1)k0` edges. In normalized incidence measure the loss is at most\n\n`k0/(p+1)+k0/p < \u03b4/50`.\n\nKeep the weaker bound that the remaining graph `G0` has edge mass at least `\u03b4/4`. It has minimum degree `k0`; its line set `L0` has normalized measure \u03bb satisfying `\u03b4/4\u2264\u03bb\u2264\u03c3`.\n\n**[P2] (proved) Support-sensitive selector.** Select each line of `L0` independently with probability `\u03b8=8/k0`. The hypothesis and `\u03c3\u2265\u03b4` imply\n\n`\u03b4\u00b2\u226510^15 d/p`,  `\u03b4p\u2265sqrt(10^15dp)>3\u00b710^9`,\n\nso `k0\u2265\u03b4p/200`. For a fixed `L\u2208L0`, coverage indicators at distinct neighbors of `L` depend on disjoint sets of other lines. Each has success probability above `3/4`; Hoeffding therefore bounds failure to cover half the neighbors by `exp(\u2212k0/8)`. Since `k0\u22658 log(4p(p+1))`, a union bound over all affine lines costs less than `1/4`.\n\nIf `r=|R|`, then `E[r]=\u03b8|L0|\u2265200(p+1)` and `Var(r)\u2264E[r]`. Chebyshev puts `r` between half and twice its mean with failure below `1/4`. Some deterministic selection consequently satisfies both coverage and\n\n`100(p+1)\u2264r\u226416|L0|/k0\u22646400\u03c3p/\u03b4`.\n\nThese are the only Hoeffding, selector union, and Chebyshev losses.\n\n**[P3] (proved) Weighted interpolation.** Give `X,Y,Z` weights `1,1,d` and set\n\n`D=16(floor(sqrt(dr))+1)`.\n\nThen `D\u00b2>256dr` and KTZ's monomial count gives `dim(V_D)\u2265D\u00b3/(64d)>r(D+1)`. Each formal identity `A(L(t),P_L(t))=0` imposes at most `D+1` coefficient equations, so a nonzero interpolant exists. Moreover,\n\n`D\u22641280 sqrt(d\u03c3p/\u03b4)+16\u22641280\u03b4p/sqrt(10^15)+16<\u03b4p/10000`.\n\nThus `D<p`, `D<k0/2`, and, for `k1=floor(\u03b4p/1000)`, `D<k1/2`. Also `r>D`. A nonzero `Z`-independent polynomial of degree at most `D` cannot vanish identically on more than `D` affine lines, so `A_Z\u22600`. Choosing minimum weighted degree removes repeated factors and makes `A` squarefree.\n\n**[P4] (proved) Identity extension and formal content removal.** Every `L\u2208L0` has more than `k0/2>D` distinct accepted points that also lie on selected accepted lines. At each such point the two line labels equal the same value `f(x)`. Hence the degree-at-most-`D` polynomial `A(L(t),P_L(t))` has more than `D` distinct roots and is identically zero.\n\nWrite `A=H(X,Y)B(X,Y,Z)`, where `H` is the gcd of the coefficients in `Z`. At most `deg(H)\u2264D` base lines satisfy `H|_L=0` identically. On every other retained line, `H(L(t))B(L(t),P_L(t))=0` in the integral domain `F_p[t]`; hence `B(L(t),P_L(t))=0`. This is formal polynomial division, not division by values of `H`. No root multiplicities are counted.\n\n**[P5] (proved) Prime vertical-derivative lemma.** Factor the squarefree primitive polynomial as `B=c\u220fP_i` into distinct irreducibles over `F_p`. Primitivity implies that every `P_i` genuinely depends on `Z`. Since `deg_Z(P_i)<p`, its derivative `(P_i)_Z` is nonzero, and its smaller degree implies `P_i` does not divide `(P_i)_Z`. Modulo `P_i`,\n\n`B_Z = (P_i)_Z \u220f_{j\u2260i}P_j \u22600`.\n\nThus no irreducible factor of `B` divides `B_Z`, proving `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`. No irreducibility over the algebraic closure is required. This replaces, in the prime-field regime only, KTZ's generic directional derivative.\n\n**[P6] (proved) Degenerate-root deletion.** Apply KTZ's resultant line bound to the coprime pair `(B,B_Z)`. Delete the at most `D` content lines, at most `D(D\u22121)` lines on which the two graph identities degenerate together, and at most `D` zeros of `B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))` on every other line. Their total normalized edge mass is bounded by\n\n`D/[p(p+1)] + D(D\u22121)/[p(p+1)] + D/p < \u03b4/16`.\n\nPruning both sides at degree `k1=floor(\u03b4p/1000)` costs at most\n\n`k1/(p+1)+k1/p<\u03b4/500`.\n\nThe surviving graph `G1` has edge mass at least `\u03b4/8`, minimum degree `k1`, and `B_Z(x,f(x))\u22600` at every surviving point. No discriminant or Markov inequality appears.\n\n**[P7] (proved) Hensel lifting and propagation.** At a surviving point translate the base coordinates to `(0,0)` and put `\u03b1=f(0,0)`. In `F_p[[X,Y]]`, construct a root `\u03a6=\u03b1+\u03a6_1+\u03a6_2+\u2026` recursively by homogeneous degree. At stage `j`, the degree-`j` residual is canceled uniquely by division by the scalar `B_Z(0,0,\u03b1)`. Thus no factorial is inverted.\n\nEvery incident line polynomial is the same unique root after restriction to that line. There are more than `D` incident directions. Therefore every homogeneous part `\u03a6_j` with `d<j\u2264D` vanishes on more than `D\u2265j` projective directions and is zero. Let `Q` be the truncation through degree `d`. The polynomial `B(X,Y,Q)` has degree at most `D` and all terms through degree `D` vanish, so it is identically zero. Simple-root uniqueness propagates the same `Q` across every edge of the connected component, and `Q=f` at all of its point vertices.\n\n**[P8] (proved) Component mixing and recovery.** For a component let `a,b,e` denote its normalized point, line, and edge measures. Put `\u03ba=k1/p` and `u=1/sqrt(p+1)`. Minimum degree and point-line mixing give\n\n`e\u2265\u03baa/2`,  `e\u2265\u03bab`,  and  `e\u2264ab+u sqrt(ab)`.\n\nThe theorem hypothesis gives `u<\u03b4/8000\u2264\u03ba/4`. If `a<\u03ba/4`, the last two inequalities imply `9b\u2264a`, which contradicts the first inequality. If `b<\u03ba/4`, they imply `a\u2264b`, which contradicts `e\u2265\u03bab`. Hence `a,b\u2265\u03ba/4\u2265\u03b4/8000`. The polynomial from [P7] therefore has global agreement at least `\u03b4/8000`. This is the sole incidence Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss.\n\n**[P9] (proved) Exact cubic reconstruction.** The dominant scales are\n\n`r=O(\u03c3p/\u03b4)`,  `D=O(sqrt(d\u03c3p/\u03b4))`,  `D=O(\u03b4p)`.\n\nThe first two give the interpolation degree; the last is independently demanded by identity extension, the `D/p` bad-incidence term, and lifting. Squaring the final comparison yields exactly `\u03b4\u00b3=\u03a9(d\u03c3/p)`. The resultant term `D\u00b2/p\u00b2` alone needs only `\u03b4\u00b2=\u03a9(d\u03c3/p)`, and mixing needs only `\u03b4=\u03a9(p^\u22121/2)`; both are weaker here. For \u03c3=1 this is the KTZ cubic exponent.\n\n**[P10] (conditional) Concentrated-carrier exponent.** If additionally `\u03c3\u2264A\u03b4`, [P9] becomes `\u03b4\u00b2=\u03a9(Ad/p)`, giving exponent `1/2`. Since every carrier has `\u03c3\u2265\u03b4`, this support-sensitive interpolation balance cannot exceed exponent `1/2`. This is not an unconditional improvement of the benchmark.\n\n**[P11] (proved) Modal occupancy lower bound.** For Theorem C choose all `p\u00b2` point values independently and uniformly. On a fixed line let `N_a` be the occupancy of value `a`, `M=max_a N_a`, and `Y=\u03a3_a 1[N_a=r]`. For one value,\n\n`Pr[N_a=r] = binom(p,r)p^(\u2212r)(1\u22121/p)^(p\u2212r) \u2265 1/(8r!)`.\n\nHere `r\u00b2\u2264p`, `(1\u22121/p)^p\u22651/4`, and `r!\u2264r^r\u2264p^(1/4)`. Thus `\u03bc=E[Y]\u2265p^(3/4)/8\u22651`. For distinct values, the joint probability of both occupancies equaling `r` is at most `1/(r!)\u00b2`, at most 64 times the product of the lower bounds. Hence `E[Y\u00b2]\u2264\u03bc+64\u03bc\u00b2\u226465\u03bc\u00b2`. Cauchy\u2013Schwarz, equivalently the zero-threshold Paley\u2013Zygmund argument, gives `Pr[Y>0]\u22651/65`, so `E[M]\u2265r/65`.\n\nGive each line a modal constant label. By linearity of expectation across lines\u2014no line independence is asserted\u2014the local agreement `A` satisfies `E[A]\u2265r/(65p)`.\n\n**[P12] (proved) Modal upper concentration.** A factorial-moment union bound gives\n\n`Pr[M\u2265s]\u2264p/s!\u2264p(e/s)^s`.\n\nFor `s0=ceil(4 log p/log log p)`, the tail sums to less than one and `E[M]\u2264s0+1\u226425r`; hence `E[A]\u226425r/p`. Changing one point value changes the modal count on only its `p+1` incident lines and changes `A` by at most `1/p\u00b2`. McDiarmid therefore gives\n\n`Pr[A>50r/p]\u2264exp(\u22121250r\u00b2)\u2264r/(520p)`.\n\nNo Markov inequality is used.\n\n**[P13] (proved) Global union bound and deterministic instance.** There are `p^N` formal total-degree-at-most-101 polynomials, with `N=5253`. For fixed `Q`, its agreement count with random `f` is `Bin(p\u00b2,1/p)`, of mean `p`. Chernoff gives\n\n`Pr[agreements(Q,f)\u22652p]\u2264(e/4)^p`.\n\nUnion over all `p^N` polynomials gives `p^N(e/4)^p\u2264exp(\u2212p/4)\u2264r/(520p)` under the stated lower bound on `p`. Let `G` be the event that all global agreements are below `2/p`, and `H={A\u226450r/p}`. Since `0\u2264A\u22641`,\n\n`E[A\u00b71_{G\u2229H}] \u2265 r/(65p)\u2212r/(520p)\u2212r/(520p) > r/(130p)`.\n\nSome deterministic table in `G\u2229H` therefore has all three bounds in Theorem C.\n\n**[P14] (refuted) Uniform exact-linear soundness.** Suppose constants `C,c>0` made `\u03b5\u2265Cd/p` imply `Agr_d(f)\u2265c\u03b5` uniformly. Fix the legal ambient cap `d=101` and choose a sufficiently large prime with `r\u2265max{130\u00b7101C,260/c}`. Theorem C then has `\u03b5\u2265C\u00b7101/p` but `Agr_101(f)<2/p<c\u03b5`, a contradiction. Thus the exact-linear statement is false. On the other hand, for each fixed `\u03b7>0`,\n\n`\u03b5/(101/p)^(1\u2212\u03b7) \u2264 50r/[101^(1\u2212\u03b7)p^\u03b7] \u2192 0`,\n\nso this construction does not refute a fixed-\u03b7 target.\n\n**[P15] (proved) Near-p information set.** Choose distinct `a_0,\u2026,a_d` and `b_0,\u2026,b_d` and the triangular set `S={(a_i,b_j):i+j\u2264d}`. The Newton products `\u220f_{h<i}(X\u2212a_h)\u220f_{k<j}(Y\u2212b_k)` with `i+j\u2264d` form a triangular evaluation basis on `S`. Hence arbitrary prescribed values on all `|S|=(d+1)(d+2)/2` points extend to a total-degree-at-most-`d` polynomial. Applying this to `f|_S` proves Proposition D. In particular, the lower bound is `(p+1)/(2p)` at `d=p\u22121` and `5253/10609` at `d=101,p=103`.\n\n**[P16] (proved) Diffuse support need not concentrate.** Fix the legal ambient `d\u2265101`, take `f=0`, and on every line choose a degree-`d` label with `d` distinct prescribed parameter roots. Then `\u03b5=d/p` and every line supports acceptance, so `\u03c3=1`; nevertheless `Q=0` agrees globally everywhere. Thus local density does not imply `\u03c3=O(\u03b5)`, although this example is harmless for soundness.\n\n**[P17] (refuted as an obstruction) Concentrated good directions.** Let `f` be a product of `d+1` distinct homogeneous linear forms. In each of the corresponding `d+1` projective directions, every affine-line restriction loses its degree-`d+1` leading term and is a legal degree-`d` label. This gives local mass about `(d+1)/(p+1)`. But `Q=0` agrees on the union of the same `d+1` lines through the origin, a \u0398(d/p) fraction. The attempted counterexample already contains the required global polynomial.\n\n**[P18] (refuted safety of omitting simplicity) Branch collision.** For odd `p` and legal ambient cap `d\u2265101`, `B=Z\u00b2\u2212X\u00b2` is squarefree but its two legal branches `Q=X` and `Q=\u2212X` meet at the origin, where `B_Z=0`. Agreement at that incidence cannot select a branch. Vertical-simple-root deletion is therefore logically necessary.\n\n**[P19] (refuted as an active obstruction) Inseparability.** A polynomial with vanishing `Z`-derivative must use positive `Z`-exponents divisible by `p`. Since the interpolant has weighted degree `D<p`, no such exponent occurs. Examples such as `Z^p\u2212G` lie outside the interpolation space and do not obstruct the prime-field proof.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Scale or loss | Consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| Carrier pruning | `<\u03b4/50`, retained as `\u03b4/4` | Constant only |\n| Selector probability | Hoeffding `e^(\u2212k0/8)`, union over `p(p+1)` | No \u03b4-power loss |\n| Selector size | Chebyshev; `r\u22646400\u03c3p/\u03b4` | One factor `\u03c3/\u03b4` |\n| Interpolation | `dim(V_D)\u2248D\u00b3/d` versus `rD` constraints | `D\u2248sqrt(dr)` |\n| Root budget | `D\u2264\u0398(\u03b4p)` | `\u03b4\u00b3=\u03a9(d\u03c3/p)` |\n| Content/resultant deletion | `D/p + D\u00b2/p\u00b2` | Cubic plus a weaker quadratic gate |\n| Second pruning | `<\u03b4/500` | Constant only |\n| Mixing | One Cauchy\u2013Schwarz error `p^\u22121/2` | Weaker than cubic for `d\u2265101` |\n| Recovery | Component point density `\u03b4/8000` | Linear global recovery |\n| Diffuse carrier | `\u03c3=1` | Exponent `1/3` |\n| Concentrated carrier | `\u03c3\u2264A\u03b4` | Conditional exponent `1/2` |\n| Modal occupancy | `r\u2248log p/(4 log log p)` | Local `\u0398(r/p)` |\n| Polynomial union | `p^5253(e/4)^p` | Global `<2/p` |\n| Exact-linear claim | Ratio at most `260/r` | Tends to zero; exponent 1 with constant threshold is false |\n\nThere is no hidden Markov loss. The only probabilistic inequalities are the selector's Hoeffding, union, and Chebyshev bounds; the modal occupancy second moment, factorial union, and McDiarmid bound; and the global Chernoff union. The sole incidence Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss is the `p^\u22121/2` mixing error.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\nThe successful adversarial table is Theorem C: it is diffuse across lines and exploits the maximum occupancy among `p` symbols, not low characteristic or a small exceptional direction set. It proves that the campaign's possible sharp threshold cannot literally be a constant multiple of `d/p` with linear recovery.\n\nThe all-lines prescribed-root table [P16] shows why line-support concentration cannot be assumed. The homogeneous-direction construction [P17] fails because its zero set already supplies a global polynomial. The branch collision [P18] validates the simple-root deletion. The inseparable attempt [P19] is excluded by `D<p`. Proposition D handles `d` near `p`; it is a positive agreement baseline, not an obstruction.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The field is exactly the prime field `F_p`; no extension-field descent is used.\n- The ambient degree always satisfies `101\u2264d<p`. Constant or linear objects appearing inside examples are legal labels or branches under that ambient cap; no test with parameter `d\u2264100` is analyzed.\n- Because `D<p`, the characteristic-pruned weighted monomial set equals the full weighted ball: every positive `Z`-exponent is strictly below `p`.\n- Lemma B rules out inseparable vertical factors after content removal. Absolute irreducibility is unnecessary.\n- KTZ's source proof uses a generic directional derivative. The replacement by `B_Z` is a new prime-field simplification and causes no exponent gain.\n- No discriminant is used. The resultant is invoked only for the proved coprime pair `(B,B_Z)`.\n- Division by `H` occurs only as an integral-domain inference on non-content lines. Hensel lifting divides only by a nonzero scalar `B_Z(x,f(x))`.\n- All interpolation constraints are coefficient identities, and every later root count uses distinct points or directions rather than multiplicity.\n- When `d` is near `p`, Theorem A's premise is vacuous because `\u03c3\u2265\u03b4` would force `p\u226510^15d`; Proposition D supplies the appropriate direct check.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe general KTZ benchmark is not improved: the exponent `1/2` conclusion requires the additional hypothesis `\u03c3=O(\u03b4)`, and diffuse carriers can have `\u03c3=1`. The constant `10^15` is deliberately conservative and is not claimed optimal.\n\nThe modal obstruction refutes a uniform constant-times-`d/p` trigger but not any fixed exponent `1\u2212\u03b7`. It instead shows that an exponent-1 formulation must include a subpolynomial occupancy allowance, at least on the order of `log p/log log p` when `d=101`.\n\nThe current selector has an upper bound `O(\u03c3p/\u03b4)`, whereas covering more than `k0/2` points on one line requires at least `\u03a9(\u03b4p)` distinct witness lines. Closing this gap demands a new combinatorial or algebraic idea. No computation, higher-dimensional lifting, extension field, or individual-degree substitution is used here.",

Therefore $Agr_d\u226413/p$, while $Acc\u2265(d+1)/p$, so the ratio is at most $13/(d+1)\u21920$.\n\n**[P15 \u2014 conditional] What sparsification alone could buy.** Suppose a replacement for Lemma 3.2 gave $|R|=O(p/\u03b5^\u03b3)$ while retaining the same coefficient-count and root-budget steps. Then\n\n$D^2\u2273dp/\u03b5^\u03b3$ and $D\u2272\u03b5p$\n\nimply $d/p\u2272\u03b5^{2+\u03b3}$, or $\u03b5\u2273\u03c1^{1/(2+\u03b3)}$. Thus $|R|=O(p)$ gives exponent $1/2$, not exponent near one. Near-linear soundness needs a family near the geometric scale $\u0398(\u03b5p)$ or a different interpolation/propagation mechanism. Theorem C shows that density and minimum degree alone cannot even provide $O(p)$ on all accepted graphs.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Pruning | $\u03b5$ | absolute constants | edge measure $\u2265\u03b5/4$, $k_0=\u0398(\u03b5p)$ |\n| Sparsification | $k_0=\u0398(\u03b5p)$ | one factor $\u03b5^{-1}$ | $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$ |\n| Interpolation | $dim(V_D)=\u03a9(D^3/d)$, $O(|R|D)$ constraints | square root | $D=O(sqrt(dp/\u03b5)+1)$ |\n| Root extension | $D<k_0/2$ | compare with $\u03b5p$ | $\u03b5^3\u2273d/p$ |\n| Trivial-line deletion | $D/p\u2264O(\u03b5)$ | compare with $\u03b5p$ | $\u03b5^3\u2273d/p$ |\n| Degenerate-line deletion | $D^2/p^2\u2264O(\u03b5)$ | quadratic term | $\u03b5^2\u2273d/p$ only |\n| Root lifting | $D<k_1/2$ | compare with $\u03b5p$ | $\u03b5^3\u2273d/p$ |\n| Formal-degree safety | $D<p$ | none beyond degree | $\u03b5\u2273d/p$ only |\n| Chernoff and mixing | $\u03b5p$, $p^{-1/2}$ | logarithmic/field-size conditions | no new $d/p$ power |\n| Propagation | one $G_1$ component | factor $1/8000$ | global agreement $\u2265\u03b5/8000$ |\n| Hypothetical $|R|=O(p/\u03b5^\u03b3)$ | same algebra | architecture conversion | exponent $1/(2+\u03b3)$ |\n| Endpoint $d=0$ | threshold zero | ratio $\u2264260/r$ | universal linear conclusion refuted |\n| Sharp-scale adversary | $\u03b5=\u0398(d/p)$ | global $O(1/p)$ | ratio $O(1/d)$ |\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Degree zero \u2014 successful.** Theorem A is a genuine counterexample to the literal target, not merely to a proof technique.\n\n2. **Random prescribed interpolation \u2014 scale obstruction.** Proposition D shows that agreement of order $d/p$ cannot by itself force a constant global/local ratio. Its agreement is far below $(d/p)^{1/3}$, so it does not challenge KTZ.\n\n3. **Diffuse random incidences \u2014 proof-method obstruction.** Theorem C matches the $p/\u03b5$ reaching-family size, but its realization has the perfect decoder $Q=0$ and $d_G=\u0398(\u03b5p)$. It cannot rule out a sparsifier exploiting the stronger cubic-regime inequality $d\u226a\u03b5p$.\n\n4. **Concentrated good directions \u2014 not extremal.** If about $\u03b5p$ whole direction classes are accepted, one complete parallel class of $p$ lines reaches every point. This replaces $p/\u03b5$ by $p$ and leads to the exponent-$1/2$ ledger, so concentration is easier than the diffuse graph.\n\n5. **Near-characteristic degree \u2014 nonvacuousness failure.** At $d=p-1$, arbitrary restrictions can be interpolated on every line. After enlarging the existential KTZ constant to $C\u22651$, however, $\u03b5\u2265C(d/p)^{1/3}$ is generally impossible near $d=p$, so this does not refute the published positive-degree statement.\n\n6. **Small fields \u2014 exact checks only.** Exhaustive enumeration at $(p,d)=(2,0),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1),(3,2)$ found worst local/global ratios $4/3,4/3,7/4,3/2,9/7$, respectively. These checks expose no additional positive-degree defect and carry no asymptotic force.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\nFor $1\u2264d<p$, the positive-degree proof is characteristic-safe. KTZ's allowed monomials omit positive $Z^k$ with $p|k$; once $D<p$, this omission is automatic because $k\u2264D/d<p$. The minimum-weight interpolant is squarefree. Since finite fields are perfect, an irreducible factor with all ordinary partial derivatives zero would be a nontrivial $p$-th power. Lemma 2.4 then chooses an $F_p$-directional derivative outside fewer than $p$ bad subspaces; this is where the strict $D<p$ matters.\n\nRevision 1 uses no discriminant and assumes no absolute irreducibility. Coprimality of $B$ and its directional derivative is sufficient for the resultant count. The factorization $A=HB$ is exact; cancellation is in $F_p[t]$, not pointwise division by $H$. After derivative-degenerate incidences are removed, $B_Z(x,f(x))$ is a nonzero field element. Newton\u2013Hensel lifting divides only by this scalar and uses no factorials. All interpolation uses ordinary coefficient constraints and distinct roots, not hidden multiplicities.\n\nAt $d=0$, by contrast, the weighted $Z$-degree is zero, Lemma 2.2's dimension bound divides by $d$, and the minimum-weight argument loses positivity. Theorem A shows that this is a genuine theorem-level defect rather than harmless notation.\n\n## Limitations\n\n- No exponent stronger than $1/3$ is proved for the corrected regime $1\u2264d<p$; therefore `benchmark_improved=false`.\n- The endpoint counterexample corrects the literal campaign statement. It should not be presented as refuting KTZ if that paper's intended convention is $d\u22651$.\n- The reaching-set obstruction applies to arguments using only incidence density and minimum degree. Its polynomial realization has a perfect global decoder and lies at $d=\u0398(\u03b5p)$, not in the cubic regime.\n- Proposition D confirms the $d/p$ scale only up to constants; it does not rule out a theorem triggered at every sufficiently large constant multiple of $d/p$.\n- Revision 1 does not publish an explicit valid threshold constant $C$, so this audit preserves its existential constant rather than importing the old cached value.\n- Finite enumeration was used only for falsification. It cannot establish asymptotic soundness.\n- No claim is made about dimensions above two, extension fields, descent, or dimension bootstrapping.",

I prove a prime-specific algebraic lemma: once the content in \\(Z\\) has been removed, every squarefree explainer \\(B\\) of \\((1,1,d)\\)-weighted degree \\(D<p\\) is automatically separable in the vertical variable, and\n\\[\n\\deg_{X,Y}\\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)\n \\le (2n-1)D-dn^2\\le D^2/d-D,\n\\]\nwhere \\(n=\\deg_Z B\\). Every line contains \\(p\\) points and every point lies on \\(p+1\\) lines. Hence choosing a uniform line and then a uniform point on it is exactly uniform incident-pair sampling. For a point table \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and arbitrary line polynomials \\(P_L\\) of degree at most \\(d\\), write\n\\[\n\\epsilon=\\operatorname{Agr}_{\\rm LVP}(f,P)\n =\\Pr_{L,\\,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n\\]\nGlobal degree always means **total degree**. A line-polynomial graph is\n\\(\\Gamma_L=\\{(L(t),p_L(t)):t\\in\\mathbb F_p\\}\\).\n\nThe case \\(d=0\\) is treated separately because the above weight gives \\(Z\\) weight zero and the unrestricted weighted interpolation space is infinite-dimensional.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe controlling source is [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download). The literature summaries were therefore used only for navigation.\n\n## Theorem\n\n### Theorem A (vertical separability and weighted resultant)\n\nLet \\(p\\) be prime, \\(1\\le d<p\\), and \\(D<p\\). Let\n\\[\nB(X,Y,Z)=\\sum_{i=0}^n b_i(X,Y)Z^i\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]\n\\]\nbe nonzero, squarefree, primitive in \\(Z\\), of positive \\(Z\\)-degree \\(n\\), and of \\((1,1,d)\\)-weighted degree at most \\(D\\). Then\n\\[\n\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1\n\\]\nand, for \\(R=\\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)\\),\n\\[\nR\\ne0,\n\\qquad\n\\deg R\\le E:=(2n-1)D-dn^2\n\\le D^2/d-D.\n\\]\n\nIf \\(\\mathcal T\\) is any family of distinct affine lines carrying degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomials with \\(B(L(t),p_L(t))\\equiv0\\), then at most \\(E\\) lines also have \\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))\\equiv0\\). On every other line there are at most \\(D-d\\) points at which \\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))=0\\). Their normalized incidence loss is at most\n\\[\n\\frac{E}{p(p+1)}+\\frac{D-d}{p}.\n\\]\nIf one first removes the \\(Z\\)-content \\(H(X,Y)\\) from an interpolant of degree at most \\(D\\), the at most \\(D\\) content-trivial lines add \\(D/[p(p+1)]\\).\n\n### Proposition B (thickened-line interpolation)\n\nLet \\(r\\) line graphs \\(\\Gamma_M\\) carry degree-at-most-\\(d\\) labels, let \\(s\\ge1\\), and let \\(W_D\\) be the full weighted-degree-at-most-\\(D\\) space. In affine coordinates \\((t,u)\\) with \\(M=\\{u=0\\}\\), put\n\\[\nI_M=(u,Z-p_M(t)).\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n\\dim W_D=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\lfloor D/d\\rfloor}\\binom{D-dj+2}{2},\n\\]\nand the codimension of \\(I_M^s\\cap W_D\\) is at most\n\\[\nJ_s(D,d)=\\sum_{a+b<s}(D-a-db+1)_+.\n\\]\nConsequently, a nonzero \\(A\\in W_D\\cap\\bigcap_M I_M^s\\) exists whenever \\(\\dim W_D>rJ_s(D,d)\\). For \\(D\\ge2d\\), it suffices that\n\\[\nD^2>16drs(s+1).\n\\]\nAt each distinct accepted crossing with a seed graph, the restriction to a target graph acquires a root of multiplicity at least \\(s\\); \\(N\\) distinct crossings force the target identity if \\(sN>D\\).\n\n### Theorem C (the legal d=0 endpoint refutes the campaign statement)\n\nFor every prime \\(p\\ge e^{64}\\), set\n\\[\nk=\\left\\lfloor\\frac{\\log p}{4\\log\\log p}\\right\\rfloor.\n\\]\nThere exist \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and a degree-zero line table such that\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Agr}_{\\rm LVP}(f,P)\\ge \\frac{k}{256p},\n\\qquad\n\\max_{\\deg Q\\le0}\\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\\le\\frac2p.\n\\]\nThe global/local ratio is at most \\(512/k=o(1)\\). Therefore no absolute \\(c>0\\) can give global agreement at least \\(c\\epsilon\\) under the trigger \\(C(d/p)^\\alpha\\) for all \\(0\\le d<p\\), for any \\(\\alpha>0\\).\n\n## Proof\n\n**[P1, proved] Weighted consequences.** Weighted degree gives \\(n\\le D/d<p\\) and \\(\\deg b_i\\le D-di\\). In particular, \\(n\\) is nonzero in \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), so \\(B_Z\\) has \\(Z\\)-degree exactly \\(n-1\\). No derivative coefficient is divided by zero.\n\n**[P2, proved] Vertical coprimality.** Suppose an irreducible \\(C\\) divides both \\(B\\) and \\(B_Z\\), and write \\(B=CE\\). Squarefreeness gives \\(C\\nmid E\\). Modulo \\(C\\),\n\\[\n0\\equiv B_Z\\equiv C_ZE,\n\\]\nso \\(C\\mid C_Z\\); degree forces \\(C_Z=0\\). Since \\(\\deg C\\le D<p\\), every positive \\(Z\\)-exponent of \\(C\\) is below \\(p\\) and has nonzero derivative. Hence \\(C\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y]\\). Then \\(C\\) divides every \\(b_i\\), contradicting primitivity. Thus \\(\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1\\).\n\n**[P3, proved] Resultant degree.** The Sylvester determinant has \\(n-1\\) rows from \\(B\\) and \\(n\\) rows from \\(B_Z\\); every monomial in \\(R\\) therefore contains \\(2n-1\\) coefficient factors. Under \\(b_i\\mapsto\\lambda^i b_i\\), one has \\(B(Z)\\mapsto B(\\lambda Z)\\) and \\(B_Z(Z)\\mapsto\\lambda B_Z(\\lambda Z)\\), so the resultant scales by \\(\\lambda^{n(n-1)+n}=\\lambda^{n^2}\\). Every resultant monomial consequently has coefficient-index sum \\(n^2\\). Since \\(\\deg b_i\\le D-di\\),\n\\[\n\\deg R\\le(2n-1)D-dn^2.\n\\]\nCoprimality makes \\(R\\ne0\\). Finally,\n\\[\nD^2/d-D-E=(D-dn)^2/d\\ge0.\n\\]\n\n**[P4, proved] Exceptional lines and points.** If both \\(B\\) and \\(B_Z\\) vanish formally on \\(\\Gamma_L\\), then \\(R(L(t))\\equiv0\\). A nonzero bivariate polynomial of degree \\(E\\) can contain at most \\(E\\) distinct affine lines, because each line equation is a distinct irreducible factor. On a remaining line, \\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))\\) is nonzero and has degree at most \\(D-d\\), hence at most \\(D-d\\) roots. Dividing the line count by \\(p(p+1)\\) and the point count by \\(p\\) gives the asserted incidence loss. This uses neither a discriminant nor a union over derivative directions.\n\n**[P5, proved] Consequence for the KTZ algebraic stage.** KTZ writes \\(A=HB\\), with \\(H\\) the gcd of the \\(Z\\)-coefficients. Their minimum interpolant is squarefree and has \\(A_Z\\ne0\\); hence \\(B\\) is primitive, squarefree, and has positive \\(Z\\)-degree. Lemma 4.1 supplies \\(D<p\\). Theorem A therefore permits using \\(B_Z\\) directly in Section 5. The bad-line term improves from \\(D(D-1)/[p(p+1)]\\) to at most \\((D^2/d-D)/[p(p+1)]\\), and the per-line point term from \\(D/p\\) to \\((D-d)/p\\). Hensel lifting divides only by retained nonzero values of \\(B_Z\\).\n\n**[P6, proved] Why the exponent does not improve.** KTZ Lemma 3.2 and Section 4 give \\(|\\mathcal R|=\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\) and \\(D=\\Theta(\\sqrt{d|\\mathcal R|})=\\Theta(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\). Formal extension, post-deletion minimum degree, and lifting require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\). Squaring and rearranging gives\n\\[\n\\frac{dp}{\\epsilon}=O(\\epsilon^2p^2)\n\\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p).\n\\]\nThe new exceptional-line term is \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\), but the remaining point term is \\((D-d)/p=\\Theta(\\sqrt{d/(\\epsilon p)})\\); asking it to be \\(O(\\epsilon)\\) gives the same cubic inequality.\n\n**[P7, proved] Thickened-line dimension count.** The filtered change of variables \\((X,Y,Z)\\leftrightarrow(t,u,Z-p_M(t))\\) preserves weighted degree. Modulo \\(I_M^s\\), the surviving basis monomials are\n\\[\nt^c u^a(Z-p_M(t))^b,\n\\qquad a+b<s,\\quad c+a+db\\le D,\n\\]\nwhich gives \\(J_s(D,d)\\). Codimensions subadd over \\(r\\) seed graphs. For \\(D\\ge2d\\), the terms \\(0\\le j\\le D/(2d)\\) show \\(\\dim W_D\\ge D^3/(16d)\\), while \\(J_s(D,d)\\le s(s+1)D\\). The displayed sufficient condition follows.\n\n**[P8, proved] Multiplicity propagation and its simple-root obstruction.** At a crossing of distinct base lines, both generators of \\(I_M\\) vanish to order at least one on the target graph. Membership in \\(I_M^s\\) therefore gives Hasse root multiplicity at least \\(s\\); \\(N\\) distinct points contribute total multiplicity at least \\(sN\\). Repeated sampled lines through the same point count only once. However, for \\(s\\ge2\\), \\(A_Z\\in I_M^{s-1}\\), so every seed root is vertically degenerate. If \\(A=HB\\) and \\(H\\) is not identically zero on \\(M\\), then \\(A_Z=HB_Z\\) still forces \\(B_Z\\) to vanish formally there. Plain multiplicity interpolation therefore cannot feed the simple-root Newton--Hensel step.\n\n**[P9, proved] Multiplicity exponent ledger.** At KTZ scale, \\(r\\le6400p/\\epsilon\\). If \\(\\epsilon p\\ge200\\), Lemma 3.2 supplies more than \\(N=\\epsilon p/400\\) distinct covered points per target line. The sufficient interpolation and propagation inequalities are\n\\[\nD^2>16drs(s+1),\\qquad D<sN.\n\\]\nThese worst-case estimates guarantee a common interval under\n\\[\n\\epsilon^3>16{,}384{,}000{,}000\\frac{s+1}{s}\\frac d p.\n\\]\nThus \\(s\\) cancels up to \\((s+1)/s\\), and this direct certificate has no exponent gain.\n\n**[P10, proved] Occupancy on one line.** Choose \\(f(x)\\) independently and uniformly in \\(\\mathbb F_p\\). On a fixed line let \\(N_a\\) be the occupancy of color \\(a\\), \\(M=\\max_aN_a\\), and \\(Y=|\\{a:N_a=k\\}|\\). For \\(p\\ge e^{64}\\), \\(k!\\le k^k\\le p^{1/4}\\), and\n\\[\n\\frac1{8k!}\\le\\Pr[N_a=k]\\le\\frac1{k!},\n\\qquad\n\\Pr[N_a=N_b=k]\\le\\frac1{k!^2}\\quad(a\\ne b).\n\\]\nThe lower bound uses \\(\\binom pkp^{-k}\\ge1/(2k!)\\) and \\((1-1/p)^p\\ge1/4\\). Hence\n\\[\n\\mathbb EY\\ge\\frac{p}{8k!},\n\\qquad\n\\mathbb EY^2\\le\\frac p{k!}+\\frac{p^2}{k!^2}\n \\le\\frac{2p^2}{k!^2}.\n\\]\nThe second-moment/Cauchy--Schwarz inequality loses the explicit factor \\(1/128\\): \\(\\Pr[Y>0]\\ge(\\mathbb EY)^2/\\mathbb EY^2\\ge1/128\\). Thus \\(\\mathbb EM\\ge k/128\\).\n\n**[P11, proved] Global balance and simultaneous existence.** For deterministic \\(f\\), let \\(A(f)\\) be the acceptance obtained by choosing a modal constant on every line. Linearity of expectation\u2014no independence between lines\u2014is enough to give \\(\\mathbb EA(f)\\ge k/(128p)\\). For a global color class \\(X_a=|f^{-1}(a)|\\sim\\operatorname{Bin}(p^2,1/p)\\), Chernoff gives \\(\\Pr[X_a>2p]\\le(e/4)^p\\). The only union bound in this proof is over the \\(p\\) colors:\n\\[\n\\Pr[\\max_aX_a>2p]\\le p(e/4)^p\\le\\frac{k}{256p}.\n\\]\nSince \\(0\\le A\\le1\\), restricting the expectation to the balance event leaves at least \\(k/(256p)\\). Some balanced \\(f\\) attains that value. No Markov loss is used.\n\n**[P12, proved] Refutation at d=0.** Choose each \\(P_L\\) to be a modal color. Its acceptance is \\(A(f)\\). Every total-degree-zero polynomial is constant, so its agreement is at most \\(2/p\\). Given proposed absolute \\(C,c>0\\), choose a sufficiently large prime with \\(k>512/c\\). The premise \\(\\epsilon\\ge C(0/p)^\\alpha=0\\) holds, but global agreement is less than \\(c\\epsilon\\). This refutes the literal cubic benchmark and, for every fixed \\(0<\\eta<1\\), the literal \\((d/p)^{1-\\eta}\\) target.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| KTZ seed selection | local agreement \\(\\epsilon\\) | \\(|\\mathcal R|=\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\) | one factor \\(\\epsilon^{-1}\\) |\n| Ordinary interpolation | \\(|V_D|=\\Theta(D^3/d)\\), \\(|\\mathcal R|(D+1)\\) constraints | \\(D^2=\\Theta(d|\\mathcal R|)\\) | \\(D=\\Theta(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\) |\n| Extension/lifting | \\(D\\) versus \\(\\Theta(\\epsilon p)\\) roots/lines | require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\) | \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\) |\n| New vertical resultant | \\(n\\le D/d\\) | at most \\(D^2/d-D\\) bad lines | normalized \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\) at KTZ scale |\n| Remaining bad points | degree \\(D-d\\) on each nonbad line | \\((D-d)/p\\) | still forces \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\) |\n| Multiplicity \\(s\\) | interpolation cost \\(\\Theta(s^2)\\), root credit \\(s\\) | \\(D\\asymp s\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon}\\), allowance \\(s\\epsilon p\\) | \\(s\\) cancels; exponent \\(1/3\\) |\n| Degree zero | \\(k=\\Theta(\\log p/\\log\\log p)\\) | local \\(\\ge k/(256p)\\), global \\(\\le2/p\\) | global/local \\(\\le512/k=o(1)\\) |\n\nKTZ Lemma 3.2 also uses a Chernoff bound, a union bound over all affine lines, and Chebyshev for \\(|\\mathcal R|\\); these produce the displayed constants but no additional power of \\(\\epsilon\\) beyond \\(|\\mathcal R|=O(p/\\epsilon)\\). Their point-line Cauchy--Schwarz mixing error is \\(1/\\sqrt{p+1}\\), required to be at most \\(\\epsilon/8000\\); for \\(d\\ge1\\) this is dominated by a sufficiently large cubic trigger. These are quoted source losses, not silently suppressed steps in the new proof.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Adversarial table, successful:** the random balanced coloring with modal constant line labels proves Theorem C. Randomness is only a probabilistic existence proof; the resulting table is deterministic.\n2. **Concentrated good direction, not a vanishing-ratio example:** for \\(d=0\\), take \\(f(x,y)=x\\). The \\(p\\) vertical lines accept everywhere with their constant labels; every other line has one occurrence of each value. The modal table has \\(\\epsilon=2/(p+1)\\), while the best global constant has agreement \\(1/p\\), a ratio \\((p+1)/(2p)>1/2\\).\n3. **Inseparability boundary, successful algebraic obstruction:** for \\(d=1,D=p\\), \\(B=Z^p-X\\) is primitive and squarefree, but \\(B_Z=0\\). Thus \\(D<p\\) cannot simply be dropped.\n4. **Multiplicity, refuted as a plug-in improvement:** the factor \\(s\\) cancels in the exponent, and \\(s\\ge2\\) destroys simple vertical roots on every seed graph.\n5. **d near p, no counterexample claimed:** every line table can interpolate arbitrary line values at \\(d=p-1\\), but this does not replace total degree by individual degree and does not itself contradict constant global agreement. For any threshold constant \\(C>1\\), the cubic premise is vacuous when \\(d/p>C^{-3}\\).\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- Theorem A is stated only over \\(\\mathbb F_p\\); no extension-field or descent claim is made.\n- The deductions \\(n<p\\) and \\(C_Z=0\\Rightarrow C\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y]\\) use \\(D<p\\). The explicit \\(Z^p-X\\) example audits sharpness.\n- No discriminant is divided by or assumed nonzero. The nonzero resultant follows from proved coprimality.\n- No irreducibility of \\(B\\) is assumed. Squarefreeness is used factor by factor; primitivity excludes an \\(X,Y\\)-only common factor.\n- Content division is safe in the integral domain \\(\\mathbb F_p[t]\\). Hensel division occurs only after retaining \\(B_Z(x,f(x))\\ne0\\).\n- The multiplicity proof uses ideal powers/Hasse multiplicity. Ordinary derivatives would be invalid for orders reaching \\(p\\), since \\((t^p)'=0\\).\n- Several lines through one point provide one distinct root, not several. Parallel lines provide no crossing. Both concentration modes are excluded from multiplicity overcounting.\n- At \\(d=0\\), the weighted monomial count \\(D^3/(64d)\\) is undefined and the \\(Z\\)-weight is zero; this matches the endpoint missed by the positive-degree proof.\n- For the smallest primes, the asymptotic counterexample is not asserted. Exhaustive checks give ratios \\(3/4\\) at \\(p=2\\) and \\(4/7\\) at \\(p=3\\). At \\(p=2,d=1\\), Theorem A only permits \\(D=1\\), where vertical differentiation is ordinary and separable.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe vertical-resultant lemma is a genuine prime-field simplification and improves one deletion term, but it leaves the cubic bottleneck intact. Proposition B is only an interpolation/root-count statement: for \\(s\\ge2\\) it does not provide the simple roots required for a global polynomial, and no single-polynomial soundness theorem follows from it. The \\(d=0\\) construction is an obstruction to the stated quantifiers, not a positive-degree lower bound. Small-field enumeration is reported only as falsification evidence and proves no asymptotic theorem.\n\nAccordingly, the sound positive-degree baseline remains KTZ's \\(1/3\\) theorem with global agreement \\(\\Omega(\\epsilon)\\), while the literal `0 <= d < p` campaign formulation is refuted and should be corrected before further exponent comparisons.",
