research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0010/response.json:159:  "note_markdown": "# Popularity-sensitive core decoding and a bounded-star-energy obstruction\n\n## Abstract\n\nFix a prime field $F_p$, dimension $m=2$, and an integer $100<d<p$. I prove an asymmetric refinement of the accepted-component decoder. If an accepted subgraph has point minimum degree $u$, line minimum degree $v$, line measure $\u03c4$, and $w=min(u,v)$, then the two conditions\n\n$$\nuv \\ge 2^{60}dp,\n\\qquad\nuw^2 \\ge 2^{60}d\u03c4p^2\n$$\n\nforce one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial to agree with the point table on at least $v/(800p)$ of all points.\n\nFor the original accepted graph, let $u_*$ be the largest point-degree threshold supporting accepted-incidence mass at least $\u03b5/2$. The component theorem implies\n\n$$\nu_*\u03b5^2 \\ge 2^{70}d\n\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\nagr(f,Q) \\ge \u03b5/12800.\n$$\n\nThus a hypothesis $u_*\\ge \u03ba \u03b5^a p$ gives the conditional threshold $\u03b5\\ge(2^{70}/\u03ba)^{1/(a+2)}(d/p)^{1/(a+2)}$. This interpolates from exponent $1/3$ at the universally available scale $u_*=\u03a9(\u03b5p)$ to exponent $1/2$ when $u_*=\u03a9(p)$. It does not improve the unconditional benchmark.\n\nI also prove a template-popularity lemma and a complementary obstruction: for every fixed star order, diffuse modal-constant tables can have star energy only $O(\u03b5^s)$ while every degree-101 global polynomial has agreement $o(\u03b5)$. Consequently, a scale-free bounded-order collision-energy increment cannot supply the missing popularity.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nThere are $p^2$ points and $p(p+1)$ affine lines. Every point lies on $p+1$ lines and every line contains $p$ points. Each affine line $L$ carries a univariate polynomial $P_L$ of degree at most the ambient integer $d$, and $f:F_p^2\\to F_p$ is the point table. The sampling rule is exactly a uniformly random affine line followed by a uniformly random point on it; equivalently, it is a uniform affine incidence. Put\n\n$$\n\u03b5=Pr_{L,\\,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n$$\n\nThe accepted graph has edge $(x,L)$ exactly when $x\\in L$ and $P_L(x)=f(x)$. All global polynomials below have total degree at most $d$.\n\nFor a subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$, let\n\n$$\nt=|T|,\n\\qquad\n\u03c4=\\frac{t}{p(p+1)},\n$$\n\nand let $u$ and $v$ denote its point-side and line-side minimum degrees, respectively. For the full accepted graph, write $a_x$ for the accepted degree of $x$ and define the absolute upper-tail incidence mass\n\n$$\n\u03b4_j=\\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)}\\sum_{x:a_x\\ge j}a_x,\n\\qquad\nu_*=max\\{j\\in\\{1,\\ldots,p+1\\}:\u03b4_j\\ge \u03b5/2\\}.\n$$\n\nWhen $\u03b5>0$, this set is nonempty. Since points below $\u03b5(p+1)/2$ carry less than half of all accepted edges,\n\n$$\nu_*\\ge \\left\\lceil\\frac{\u03b5(p+1)}2\\right\\rceil.\n$$\n\nFor $s\\ge2$, $\u0393_s$ denotes the probability that $s$ ordered distinct uniformly sampled lines through a uniform point all accept there.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe exact benchmark is Theorem 1.1 of [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, $\u03b5\\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}$ implies one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $c\u03b5$. The following explanation of the exponent is my reconstruction, not a separately quoted theorem: their Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$, Lemma 2.2 gives an explainer degree $D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\u03b5})$, and identity extension and lifting require $D=O(\u03b5p)$. Hence $\u03b5^3=\u03a9(d/p)$.\n\nThe present proof uses KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.1--2.3, 2.5--2.7, 6.1, and 6.3. The local cached KTZ file is the earlier July 2026 version; theorem numbering is stable, but the revision above is the pinned source. The cached Arora--Sudan file is the STOC 1997 version rather than the Combinatorica 2003 article recorded in the bibliography, and no theorem-number transfer from that cache is used.\n\nThe durable corpus was audited through [DATA_MANIFEST.json](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json), all eight active campaign-10 submissions, their verifier audits, all active leaderboards, and the empty campaign-300 leaderboards; directories named `superseded` were excluded. The main reusable prior result is the verifier-accepted symmetric component theorem in [researcher-0002](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0002/note.md). The exact pair-collision and regular-carrier obstruction in [researcher-0008](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0008/note.md) shows that graph regularity alone gives no energy surplus. The verified singular-lift obstruction in [researcher-0006](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0006/note.md) remains relevant to any future factorwise refinement.\n\nFor historical comparison only, Theorem 4.2 of [Harsha--Kumar--Saptharishi--Sudan, arXiv v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12752) states the bivariate condition $p>Cd/\u03b5^7$. It is not used in the proof.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A (proved asymmetric core decoder).** Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a nonempty accepted subgraph. Suppose every $x\\in X$ has degree at least the integer $u$, every $L\\in T$ has degree at least the integer $v$, $\u03c4=|T|/[p(p+1)]$, and $w=min(u,v)$. If\n\n$$\nuv\\ge2^{60}dp,\n\\qquad\nuw^2\\ge2^{60}d\u03c4p^2,\n$$\n\nthen there is a single $Q\\in F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying\n\n$$\nPr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\\ge\\frac{v}{800p}.\n$$\n\nConnectedness of the input is not required.\n\n**Corollary B (proved implication; conditional exponent).** With $u_*$ defined above, if\n\n$$\nu_*\u03b5^2\\ge2^{70}d,\n$$\n\nthen some total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial satisfies $agr(f,Q)\\ge \u03b5/12800$. More generally, if $0\\le a\\le1$, $0<\u03ba\\le1$, and $u_*\\ge \u03ba \u03b5^a p$, then the conclusion holds whenever\n\n$$\n\u03b5\\ge\\left(\\frac{2^{70}}\u03ba\\right)^{1/(a+2)}\n       \\left(\\frac dp\\right)^{1/(a+2)}.\n$$\n\nThe exponent improvement for $a<1$ is conditional because no such popularity tail is known for every table.\n\n**Lemma C (proved template popularity).** Let $T_1,\\ldots,T_R$ be disjoint line families and let $Q_1,\\ldots,Q_R$ be total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials such that $P_L=Q_j|_L$ for $L\\in T_j$. Let $\u03c4_j=|T_j|/[p(p+1)]$, $\u03c4=\\sum_j\u03c4_j$, let $\u03b4>0$ be the normalized accepted-incidence mass on their union, and put $\u03b1=max_j agr(f,Q_j)$. Then\n\n$$\n\u03b4\\le \u03b1\u03c4+\\sqrt{\\frac{R\u03b1\u03c4}{p+1}}.\n$$\n\nIn particular, $R\\le\u03b4(p+1)$ implies $\u03b1\\ge\u03b4/4$.\n\n**Proposition D (proved bounded-star-energy obstruction).** Fix $S\\ge2$. For all sufficiently large primes $p$, at the legal ambient degree $d=101$ there is a deterministic table using constant line polynomials such that, for\n\n$$\nr=\\left\\lfloor\\frac{\\log p}{4\\log\\log p}\\right\\rfloor,\n$$\n\none has\n\n$$\n\\frac{r}{130p}\\le \u03b5\\le\\frac{26r}{p},\n\\qquad\nmax_{deg Q\\le101}agr(f,Q)<\\frac2p,\n$$\n\nand, simultaneously for $2\\le s\\le S$,\n\n$$\n\u0393_s\\le2^{s+2}(S-1)\u03b5^s.\n$$\n\nA fully explicit sufficient meaning of sufficiently large is obtained by setting $u_0=\\lceil4\\log p/\\log\\log p\\rceil$ and $v_0=\\lceil8\\log p/\\log\\log p\\rceil$ and requiring\n\n$$\nr\\ge133,\n\\quad r^2\\le p,\n\\quad p\\ge8r!,\n\\quad u_0+1\\le17r,\n\\quad v_0\\le33r,\n$$\n\n$$\n\\frac{2p}{(u_0+1)!}\\le1,\n\\quad\n\\frac{2p^3}{v_0!}\\le\\frac18,\n\\quad\np^{5253}(e/4)^p\\le\\frac18,\n\\quad\nS\\le p+1.\n$$\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved: asymmetric mixing).** Put $\u03be=|X|/p^2$, $\u03c1=|E|/[p^2(p+1)]$, $\u03b1_0=u/(p+1)$, $\u03b2_0=v/p$, and $\u03bb=(p+1)^{-1/2}$. Minimum degree and KTZ Lemma 2.1 give\n\n$$\n\u03b1_0\u03be\\le\u03c1,\n\\qquad\n\u03b2_0\u03c4\\le\u03c1,\n\\qquad\n\u03c1\\le\u03be\u03c4+\u03bb\\sqrt{\u03be\u03c4}.\n$$\n\nIf $\u03c4<\u03b1_0/4$, the first and third inequalities imply $\u03be<(16/9)\u03bb^2\u03c4/\u03b1_0^2$. Substitution into the third inequality and comparison with $\u03b2_0\u03c4\\le\u03c1$ give $\u03b1_0\u03b2_0<2\u03bb^2$, or $uv<2p$. This contradicts the first hypothesis. The symmetric calculation gives\n\n$$\n\u03c4\\ge\\frac{u}{4(p+1)},\n\\qquad\n\u03be\\ge\\frac{v}{4p}.\n$$\n\nThus $t\\ge up/4$. Substituting the line-measure bound into the second hypothesis yields\n\n$$\nw^2\\ge\\frac{2^{60}dp^2}{4(p+1)}\\ge2^{57}dp.\n$$\n\nThis last inequality, rather than an unstated fixed-$d$ assumption, supplies all logarithmic room below.\n\n**[P2] (proved: selector and probability losses).** The first hypothesis and $v\\le p$ give $u>8$. Select every line of $T$ independently with probability $8/u$. A point accepted on a target line $L$ is called reached only through a selected line in $R$ other than $L$. It has at least $u-1$ eligible lines, so its reach probability exceeds $3/4$. For distinct points of $L$, the eligible line sets are disjoint because two distinct points determine their unique common line, which is the excluded line $L$. Chernoff therefore bounds the probability that at most half of $N_G(L)$ is reached by $e^{-v/24}$.\n\nSince $v\\ge w\\ge\\sqrt{2^{57}dp}$, $2p^2e^{-v/24}<1/4$; this accounts explicitly for the union bound over all target lines. The sample-size mean is $8t/u\\ge2p$. Its lower- and upper-tail Chernoff bounds are respectively at most $e^{-p/4}$ and $e^{-2p/3}$. Hence some choice has\n\n$$\n\\frac{4t}{u}\\le r=|R|\\le\\frac{16t}{u}\n$$\n\nand reaches more than half of every line's accepted points. In particular, $r\\ge p$.\n\n**[P3] (proved: interpolation).** Set\n\n$$\nD=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{dr}\\rfloor+1).\n$$\n\nThen $D^2>256dr$ and\n\n$$\nD^2\\le1024dr\n \\le2^{14}\\frac{dt}{u}\n \\le2^{15}\\frac{d\u03c4p^2}{u}\n \\le2^{-45}w^2.\n$$\n\nThus $D<w/5000$, $D<p$, and $r\\ge p>D$. KTZ Lemma 2.2 gives $dim V_D\\ge D^3/(64d)>r(D+1)$. Each formal identity on a selected line costs at most $D+1$ homogeneous conditions, so a nonzero candidate in $V_D$ exists. If it were Z-independent, KTZ Lemma 2.5 and $r>D$ would force it to vanish identically. Its allowed positive Z-exponents are not divisible by $p$, so its Z-derivative is nonzero.\n\nLet $S_R$ be the finite union of the selected polynomial graphs and choose a nonzero polynomial $A$ of minimum weighted degree among polynomials vanishing on $S_R$ with $A_Z\\ne0$. KTZ Lemma 2.3 makes $A$ squarefree. Its weight is at most $D<p$, so pointwise vanishing at all $p$ parameters on a selected line is a formal identity. This also explains why repeated-factor removal cannot lose the line identities.\n\n**[P4] (proved: identity extension).** Every $L\\in T$ has more than $v/2>D$ accepted points reached through a selected $M\\ne L$. At such a point,\n\n$$\nP_L(x)=f(x)=P_M(x),\n$$\n\nso $A(x,P_L(x))=0$. The restricted polynomial $A(L(t),P_L(t))$ has degree at most $D$ and more than $D$ roots; hence it vanishes formally. There is no Markov or multiplicity loss at this step.\n\n**[P5] (proved: prime-field simple-root cleanup).** Write $A=HB$, where $H(X,Y)$ is the gcd of the Z-coefficients of $A$. At most $D$ affine lines are contained in $H=0$. On every other line, division in the integral domain $F_p[t]$ gives $B(L(t),P_L(t))\\equiv0$. The polynomial $B$ is squarefree, Z-primitive, Z-dependent, and has degree below $p$.\n\nMoreover, $gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Indeed, if an irreducible $C$ divided both, squarefreeness and reduction of $(CE)_Z$ modulo $C$ would give $C|C_Z$, hence $C_Z=0$. Since $deg_Z C<p$, this makes $C$ Z-independent, contradicting Z-primitivity. KTZ Lemma 2.6 now bounds the lines on whose graphs both $B$ and $B_Z$ vanish by $D(D-1)$. On every other line, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$, so it has at most $D$ accepted roots. Thus at most\n\n$$\npD^2+Dt\n$$\n\naccepted edges are deleted. No discriminant or derivative is divided by.\n\n**[P6] (proved: asymmetric pruning).** Since $|E|\\ge vt$,\n\n$$\n\\frac{pD^2+Dt}{|E|}\n \\le\\frac Dv+\\frac{pD^2}{vt}\n \\le\\frac Dv+\\frac{2^{14}dp}{uv}\n <\\frac1{4000}.\n$$\n\nLet $u_1=\\lfloor u/100\\rfloor$ and $v_1=\\lfloor v/100\\rfloor$. Iteratively delete point vertices of current degree below $u_1$ and line vertices below $v_1$. This costs less than\n\n$$\nu_1|X|+v_1|T|\\le |E|/50.\n$$\n\nA nonempty graph remains. The hypotheses imply $u_1\\ge u/200$, $v_1\\ge v/200$, and $u_1,v_1>D$.\n\n**[P7] (proved: lift, propagate, recover measure).** Every surviving point is incident to an identity line and hence satisfies $B(x,f(x))=0$; retained edges also certify $B_Z(x,f(x))\\ne0$. At a point in any surviving connected component, more than $D$ incident line roots satisfy the hypotheses of KTZ Lemma 6.1. It produces one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ with $B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\\equiv0$. The one-variable simple-root uniqueness used in KTZ Lemma 6.3 propagates this same $Q$ through the component.\n\nSince $u_1v_1\\ge uv/40000>2p$, [P1]'s asymmetric mixing calculation applied to this component gives point density at least\n\n$$\n\\frac{v_1}{4p}\\ge\\frac{v}{800p}.\n$$\n\nThe polynomial agrees with $f$ at every point of that component, proving Theorem A. There is no list-size or factor-count loss.\n\n**[P8] (conditional: popularity-tail translation).** Let $\u03b4_*=\u03b4_{u_*}\\ge\u03b5/2$ and retain all accepted edges incident to points of degree at least $u_*$. Their number is $E_*=\u03b4_*p^2(p+1)$. Peel point degrees below $U=\\lfloor u_*/2\\rfloor$ and line degrees below $V=\\lfloor\u03b4_*p/4\\rfloor$. Point deletions cost at most $E_*/2$, and line deletions cost at most\n\n$$\nVp(p+1)\\le E_*/4.\n$$\n\nThus a nonempty core remains. Under $u_*\u03b5^2\\ge2^{70}d$, floors give\n\n$$\nU\\ge u_*/3,\n\\qquad\nV\\ge\u03b4_*p/8\\ge\u03b5p/16,\n\\qquad\nmin(U,V)\\ge\u03b5p/16.\n$$\n\nConsequently,\n\n$$\nUV\\ge u_*\u03b5p/48>2^{60}dp\n$$\n\nand, for every component line measure $\u03c4_C\\le1$,\n\n$$\nUmin(U,V)^2\n \\ge u_*\u03b5^2p^2/768\n >2^{60}d\u03c4_Cp^2.\n$$\n\nTheorem A gives agreement at least $V/(800p)\\ge\u03b5/12800$. If $u_*\\ge\u03ba \u03b5^a p$, the displayed hypothesis follows from $\u03ba \u03b5^{a+2}p\\ge2^{70}d$. Universally $u_*\\ge\u03b5p/2$, so this recovers exponent $1/3$ with a large constant. For $a<1$ it is a genuine conditional improvement; $a=0$ gives exponent $1/2$.\n\n**[P9] (proved: template popularity).** Put $S_j=\\{x:Q_j(x)=f(x)\\}$ and $\u03b1_j=|S_j|/p^2$. I prove an exact weighted codimension formula for order-`s` vanishing on a lifted line-polynomial graph. It gives a characteristic-free transfer rule: `n` distinct accepted crossings force a target-line identity when `sn>D`. For one lifted degree-at-most-`d` graph,\n\n`codim_{W_D}(W_D intersect I_M^s)=c_{d,s}(D)`, where\n\n`c_{d,s}(D)=sum_{a,b>=0, a+b<s} max{D-a-db+1,0}`.\n\nConsequently, for `r` lifted graphs there is a nonzero\n\n`A in W_D intersect (intersection_M I_M^s)`\n\nwhenever `N_d(D)>r c_{d,s}(D)`. If `D>=d(s-1)`, then exactly\n\n`c_{d,s}(D)=[s(s+1)/2](D+1)-(1+d)binom(s+1,3)`.\n\nFor `D>=1`, the explicit inequality\n\n`D^2>16 d r s(s+1)`\n\nis sufficient. Thus\n\n`D0=floor(4 sqrt(d r s(s+1)))+1`\n\nworks and satisfies\n\n`D0/s<=4 sqrt(d r (s+1)/s)+1/s<=4 sqrt(2dr)+1`.\n\nConversely, in the regular certificate regime `D>=2d(s-1)` and `D>=max{d,2}`, the numerical inequality `N_d(D)>r c_{d,s}(D)` forces\n\n`D/s>(1/4)sqrt(dr)`.\n\nThis converse concerns the standard codimension-sum certificate, not the true intersection dimension: constraints from different graphs may overlap.\n\nIf a target line has `n` distinct accepted crossings with seed graphs different from it, then every such `A` restricts identically to the target graph whenever the strict inequality `sn>D` holds.\n\nFor `s>=2`, let `A=HB`, where `H(X,Y)` is the gcd of the `Z`-coefficients. On every seed line on which `H` is not formally zero, `B` still belongs to `I_M^s`; hence `B_Z` and all other first partials vanish on the graph. Coefficient-gcd cancellation therefore does not supply the simple roots required by KTZ.\n\nAs a fully quantified KTZ-scale corollary, suppose its covering lemma supplies `r<=6400p/epsilon` and more than `epsilon p/400` distinct crossings per target line, with `epsilon p>=800`. If\n\n`epsilon^3>131072000000(d/p)`,\n\nthen the above choice of `D0` satisfies `D0/s<epsilon p/400`, so multiplicity transfer succeeds. The sufficient condition is still cubic and yields only formal target-line identities, not a global polynomial.\n\n### Theorem B: the legal degree-zero endpoint is a counterexample\n\nFor every integer `k>=2` and every prime `p>=max{50,8k!}`, there exist `f:F_p^2->F_p` and a degree-zero line table such that\n\n`epsilon>=k/(4p)` and `delta_0(f)<=2/p`.\n\nThus `delta_0(f)/epsilon<=8/k`. Since `k` is arbitrary, the campaign statement over the literal range `0<=d<p` is false at `d=0`, for both the cubic benchmark and every proposed `(d/p)^(1-eta)` trigger.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1 — proved].** There are `p(p+1)` affine lines, `p` points per line, and `p+1` lines through every point. A line-point incidence therefore has probability `1/[p^2(p+1)]` under either uniform incident-pair description. No sampling model is changed.\n\n**[P2 — proved].** Choose affine coordinates `T,U` such that `T` is the fixed parameter on `M` and `M={U=0}`. The triangular change\n\n`(X,Y,Z) <-> (T,U,V=Z-p_M(T))`\n\npreserves the weighted filtration in both directions: `T,U` and the inverse affine coordinates have weight at most one, while both `V=Z-p_M(T)` and `Z=V+p_M(T)` have weight at most `d`. Thus monomials `T^i U^a V^b` with `i+a+db<=D` form a basis of `W_D`, proving the displayed formula for `N_d(D)`.\n\n**[P3 — proved].** In the new coordinates `I_M=(U,V)`. Modulo `I_M^s`, the surviving weighted monomials are exactly\n\n`T^i U^a V^b`, with `a+b<s` and `i+a+db<=D`.\n\nFor fixed `a,b`, there are `max{D-a-db+1,0}` choices of `i`. This proves the exact codimension formula. When `D>=d(s-1)`, every summand is positive; summing `a` and `b` over the triangular index set gives `binom(s+1,3)` for each, yielding the closed form.\n\n**[P4 — proved].** Codimensions of kernels subadd, so `N_d(D)>r c_{d,s}(D)` leaves a nonzero simultaneous interpolant. For `D>=1`,\n\n`N_d(D)>=D^3/(16d)` and `c_{d,s}(D)<=s(s+1)D`.\n\nIndeed, the terms with `0<=h<=floor(D/(2d))` each contribute at least `D^2/8` monomials, and there are at least `D/(2d)` such terms. The sufficient quadratic inequality follows. For the converse certificate bound, `D>=2d(s-1)` makes every one of the `s(s+1)/2` relevant summands at least `D/2`, so `c_{d,s}(D)>=s(s+1)D/4`. When also `D>=max{d,2}`, the exact dimension satisfies `N_d(D)<=4D^3/d`. Hence the certificate inequality forces `D^2>drs(s+1)/16`.\n\n**[P5 — proved].** Let a seed line `M` and a different target line `L` meet at an accepted point `L(t_x)`. Pullback to the target graph sends `U_M` to a nonzero affine polynomial vanishing at `t_x`, and sends `V_M` to `P_L(t)-P_M(T_M(L(t)))`, which also vanishes there. Both are divisible by `t-t_x`; hence `I_M^s` pulls back into `(t-t_x)^s`. Distinct crossings give distinct factors. Since weighted degree at most `D` makes `A(L(t),P_L(t))` a univariate polynomial of degree at most `D`, total root multiplicity `sn>D` forces the restriction to be identically zero. This divisibility proof is valid even when `s>=p`.\n\n**[P6 — proved, method-level].** Put `D0=floor(4 sqrt(drs(s+1)))+1`. By [P4] an interpolant exists, while\n\n`D0/s<=4 sqrt(2dr)+1<=4 sqrt(12800dp/epsilon)+1`\n\nunder `r<=6400p/epsilon`. If `epsilon p>=800`, then `1<=epsilon p/800`. The inequality\n\n`epsilon^3>131072000000(d/p)`\n\nis exactly the square of\n\n`4 sqrt(12800dp/epsilon)<epsilon p/800`.\n\nThus `D0/s<epsilon p/400`, below the KTZ crossing budget. The factor `s` has canceled. This proves a cubic identity-extension certificate only; it does not prove soundness.\n\n**[P7 — proved].** After the filtered automorphism, `I_M^s=(U,V)^s` is `I_M`-primary. One direct proof uses normal degree: the associated graded ring is `F_p[T][U,V]`, a domain, so an element of normal order zero cannot raise another element's normal order. If `A=HB` and `H` does not vanish formally on the base line, then `H` has normal order zero. Therefore `HB in I_M^s` implies `B in I_M^s`. This is exact polynomial cancellation; no value of `H` is divided by.\n\n**[P8 — proved].** Formal differentiation lowers ideal order by at most one. Thus, for `s>=2`, every first partial of `B` belongs to `I_M^(s-1)` and vanishes on the seed graph; in particular `B_Z=0` there. Equivalently, `B(M(t),Z)` is divisible by `(Z-P_M(t))^s`, so its vertical resultant with `B_Z` vanishes along that line. Squarefreeness does not help: `U^s+V^(s+1)` belongs to `(U,V)^s`, is singular along `U=V=0`, and is squarefree in every characteristic because one of `s,s+1` is nonzero modulo `p`, while neither `U` nor `V` divides the polynomial. Removing repeated factors also need not preserve membership in `I_M^s`.\n\n**[P9 — proved].** For Theorem B, choose all `p^2` values of `f` independently and uniformly. On a fixed line let `N_a` be the occupancy of color `a`, `M=max_a N_a`, and let `Y` count colors occurring exactly `k` times. For one color,\n\n`a=Pr[N_a=k]=binom(p,k)p^(-k)(1-1/p)^(p-k)>=1/(8k!)`.\n\nThe product representation of the binomial coefficient is at least `1/2`, while `(1-1/p)^(p-k)>=1/4`. Hence `mu=E[Y]=pa>=1`. For two distinct colors, the exact joint-occupancy ratio satisfies\n\n`b/a^2=[binom(p-k,k)/binom(p,k)] [(1-2/p)^(p-2k)/(1-1/p)^(2p-2k)]<= (1-1/p)^(-2k)<2`.\n\nThe last inequality follows from `p>=8k!>=8k`. Therefore `E[Y^2]<=mu+2mu^2`, and Cauchy--Schwarz gives\n\n`Pr[M>=k]>=Pr[Y>0]>=mu^2/E[Y^2]>=1/3`.\n\nNotice that the first two events are not asserted equal. Consequently `E[M]>=k/3`.\n\n**[P10 — proved].** Label each line by a modal color and let `A(f)` be the resulting local agreement. Linearity of expectation, without any independence between intersecting lines, gives `E[A]>=k/(3p)`. Let `G` be the event that every global color class has size at most `2p`. Each class size is `Bin(p^2,1/p)`, so Chernoff and the sole union bound in this construction give\n\n`Pr[G^c]<=p(e/4)^p<=k/(12p)`\n\nfor `p>=50`. Since `0<=A<=1`,\n\n`E[A 1_G]>=E[A]-Pr[G^c]>=k/(4p)`.\n\nThus some deterministic table simultaneously lies in `G` and has local agreement at least `k/(4p)`. This argument never conditions a line's occupancy distribution on `G`, and it uses no Chernoff bound for the dependent good-line indicators.\n\n**[P11 — refuted].** On `G`, every total-degree-zero polynomial is a constant and has agreement at most `2p/p^2=2/p`. Hence global/local is at most `8/k`. Given any proposed absolute recovery constant `c>0`, choose `k>8/c` and then a prime above `max{50,8k!}`. At `d=0`, the premise `epsilon>=C(d/p)^alpha` is automatic for every `alpha>0`, but `delta_0<c epsilon`. This refutes the literal universal conclusion.\n\n**[P12 — proved].** The derivative boundary is genuine: at `d=1,D=p`, `Z^p-X` is squarefree because its `X`-derivative is `-1`, but its vertical derivative is zero. Exact substitution in the formulas gives `(N,c)=(4,4),(10,7),(7,6),(35,13),(16,10)` for the five small parameter tuples reported below. These checks validate the count but have no asymptotic force.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input scale | Loss | Output scale | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| KTZ pruning | `epsilon` | floors and constants | `n>epsilon p/400` for `epsilon p>=200` | proved |\n| Reference sampling | `epsilon` | one `epsilon^(-1)` | `r<=6400p/epsilon` | quoted/proved |\n| Order-`s` graph jets | `N=Omega(D^3/d)` versus `O(rs^2D)` conditions | square root and `s^2` | `D/s=O(sqrt(dr))` | proved |\n| Regular certificate lower bound | `N>rc` | applies only when `D>=2d(s-1)` | `D/s>sqrt(dr)/4` | proved |\n| Root transfer | `n` distinct crossings | root credit `s` | require `n>D/s` | proved |\n| KTZ balance | `r<=6400p/epsilon`, `n>epsilon p/400` | `s` cancels | `epsilon^3>131072000000 d/p` suffices | proved |\n| Ordinary KTZ balance | `D_KTZ=Theta(sqrt(dp/epsilon))` | compare with `Theta(epsilon p)` | `epsilon^3=Omega(d/p)` | reconstructed/proved |\n| Degree safety | `D=O(s sqrt(dp/epsilon))` | require `D<p` downstream | extra restriction on `s`; no gain | proved |\n| Simple-root interface | `s>=2` | all first derivatives vanish on seeds | direct Hensel continuation fails | proved |\n| Source concentration/mixing | `epsilon p`, `p^(-1/2)` | logarithmic/additive only | no new power of `d/p` | quoted/proved |\n| Degree-zero line occupancy | `p` balls in `p` colors | second-moment factor `1/3` | expected local at least `k/(3p)` | proved |\n| Global balance | `p` color classes | union factor `p`, expectation subtraction | local at least `k/(4p)`, global at most `2/p` | proved |\n| Endpoint ratio | preceding row | factor `8/k` | global/local tends to zero | refuted benchmark |\n\nNo Markov inequality is used in the new argument. The only new Cauchy--Schwarz loss is the explicit `1/3` line-occupancy factor, and the only new union bound is over the `p` global colors. In KTZ, the Chernoff union over all lines needs `epsilon p` larger than a logarithm, and affine-plane mixing costs `O(p^(-1/2))`; both are dominated by a sufficiently large positive-degree cubic trigger.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Degree zero, successful.** Theorem B is a deterministic instance obtained probabilistically and refutes the campaign's literal endpoint.\n\n2. **Concentrated good directions, not a soundness counterexample.** Set `f=0`, label all lines in `r` direction classes by zero, and all other lines by one. Then `epsilon=r/(p+1)`, but every point supports exactly `r` accepted incidences and the global polynomial zero agrees everywhere. Thus one cannot assume the accepted-point support has size `O(epsilon p^2)`.\n\n3. **A nonlinear point table, unsuccessful.** For `d<=p-2`, take `f(x,y)=x^(d+1)`. Vertical lines can agree everywhere; on every nonvertical line, cancel the leading term by a product with `d+1` selected roots to obtain a degree-`d` label agreeing at those roots. This gives local agreement `(d+2)/(p+1)`. But a degree-`d` univariate interpolant agrees with `f` on `d+1` complete columns, giving global agreement at least `(d+1)/p`; the example has no vanishing global/local ratio.\n\n4. **Squarefree jets, unsuccessful as a repair.** `U^s+V^(s+1)` is squarefree but still singular on the whole seed graph. Squarefreeness and irreducibility heuristics do not restore a simple vertical root.\n\n5. **Inseparability, successful as a boundary check.** `Z^p-X` shows that `D<p` cannot be silently removed from vertical-derivative arguments.\n\n6. **Near-characteristic degree.** At `d=p-1,D=p-1,s=2`, the dimension count handles fewer than roughly `p/4` arbitrary graphs, while KTZ selects at least `100p`; large multiplicity is therefore especially unhelpful near `d=p`. A sufficiently large benchmark constant makes this parameter range vacuous rather than proving a new theorem there.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The graph-jet interpolation and transfer statements are over the prime field and make no extension-field or descent claim.\n- The ideal-power proof uses divisibility, equivalently Hasse multiplicity, and remains sound for `s>=p`. Ordinary higher derivatives would miss terms such as `V^p`.\n- Although `d<p`, the auxiliary `D` can exceed `p`. KTZ's derivative-selection lemma cannot then be imported without an additional argument.\n- No discriminant is assumed nonzero. For `s>=2`, the vertical resultant or discriminant is instead forced to vanish along every nontrivial seed graph.\n- No explainer is assumed irreducible. The primaryness of `(U,V)^s` is proved through its normal-degree filtration.\n- Coefficient-gcd cancellation takes place in a polynomial ring; there is no division by a value that could vanish.\n- Each distinct target point contributes one root, regardless of how many seed lines pass through it. Parallel seed lines contribute no target crossing.\n- At `d=0`, weight zero on `Z` makes the interpolation space infinite-dimensional. The separate counterexample shows this is a theorem-level endpoint issue, not harmless notation.\n- Exhaustive degree-zero checks give minimum global/local ratios `3/4` at `p=2` and `4/7` at `p=3`. The asymptotic construction is not claimed for these primes.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe exact count proves an obstruction only to the natural uniform ideal-power upgrade coupled to the existing reference-family and root-count architecture. Dependencies among constraints could reduce the true intersection codimension, and a nonuniform or transverse multiplicity scheme could behave differently.\n\nThe jet lemma produces formal line identities, not a single global polynomial. For `s>=2`, its roots are precisely unsuitable for the current simple-root Newton-Hensel step. A replacement multiple-root continuation theorem would be needed before any soundness conclusion.\n\nThe degree-zero construction refutes the campaign's explicit quantifiers, but it should not be advertised as refuting KTZ if their intended convention was positive degree. After correcting to `1<=d<p`, no exponent beyond `1/3` is proved here. The prior positive-degree counterexamples and sparsifier barriers remained unverified at the corpus cutoff and are reported only as pending results.\n\nFinite-field computation was used only to check small cases. No claim concerns `m>2`, extension fields, descent, individual degree, axis-parallel sampling, or a list of candidate global polynomials." ,"obstructions":["At d=0 the benchmark threshold is zero, yet local modal agreement can exceed the best global constant agreement by an arbitrarily large factor.","Uniform order-s graph jets cost Theta(s^2D) constraints per graph while providing only s-fold root credit, so s cancels in the interpolation/root-budget balance.","For s>=2 every nontrivial seed graph remains vertically singular after coefficient-gcd cancellation; the current simple-root Newton-Hensel step cannot start.","The auxiliary degree grows linearly with s, so the required D<p separability range becomes harder to maintain.","Codimension subadditivity can be loose because graph constraints may overlap; the result does not exclude a method exploiting such dependencies.","Concentrated-direction examples show that accepted-point support need not shrink with epsilon.","Pending corpus constructions suggest the Omega(p/epsilon) reference size may be incidence-optimal, but this is not imported without verification."],"parameter_regime":"Dimension m=2. Instead, two bottlenecks are resolved negatively. First, the parameter range in the workspace, $0≤d<p$, makes the advertised theorem false at $d=0$: for all sufficiently large primes there are constant line tables with local agreement $Ω(log p/(p log log p))$ while every global constant agrees on only $O(1/p)$ of the plane. A union bound over all degree-$d$ polynomials extends this obstruction to a growing positive-degree regime and refutes a bare $C d/p$ threshold with linear global agreement, although it does not refute the fixed-$η$ target $(d/p)^{1-η}$.\n\nSecond, an explicit genuine degree-$(k-1)$ line table realizes a regular accepted-incidence graph for which every KTZ-style family that witnesses a constant fraction of the accepted incidences must contain $Ω(p/ε)$ lines. Thus the concentration size used by KTZ is optimal if the step sees only the accepted graph. Combining that unavoidable size with their interpolation degree and root budget reproduces the cubic barrier. Any exponent improvement must therefore exploit the polynomial labels before or during sparsification.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix dimension $m=2$ and a prime $p$. Let $L_p$ be the $p(p+1)$ affine lines of $F_p^2$. Each line has $p$ points, so there are $p^2(p+1)$ incident pairs. Sampling is exactly uniform in $L∈L_p$ and then uniform in $x∈L$.\n\nFor a point table $f:F_p^2→F_p$ and line polynomials $P_L$ of degree at most $d<p$, write\n\n$$\na=Pr_{L,x∈L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]\n$$\n\nfor actual local agreement, and\n\n$$\nδ_d(f)=max_{deg Q≤d}Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\n$$\n\nfor best total-degree-$d$ global agreement. No individual-degree convention is used.\n\nFor an accepted incidence graph $E$, a KTZ-style family $R$ covers an accepted edge $(x,L)$ only when there is another line $M∈R\\{L}$ with $(x,M)∈E$. This exclusion of $L$ itself is the witness convention in KTZ Lemma 3.2.\n\n## Prior Results\n\n[KTZ Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download) states the cubic threshold over arbitrary finite fields and arbitrary line tables. In its bivariate proof the final agreement is explicitly at least $ε/8000$. Its concentration step is Lemma 3.2: after pruning to minimum degree $k_0=Θ(εp)$, it samples a line family of size $O(p/ε)$ that reaches more than half the accepted points on every surviving line. Section 4 then takes $D=Θ(sqrt(d|R|))$, and Lemma 4.1 requires $D<Θ(εp)$.\n\nThe exponent $1/3$ is my reconstruction from those quoted lemmas, not a separately quoted KTZ statement:\n\n$$\n|R|=O(p/ε),\\quad D=O(sqrt(dp/ε)),\\quad D=O(εp)\n$$\n\nimply $ε^3=Ω(d/p)$. The Chernoff union bound in Lemma 3.2 only requires $εp=Ω(log p)$ and does not itself create the cubic power.\n\nThere is a scope defect at $d=0$. No positive-degree hypothesis appears before the printed theorem, but KTZ Lemma 2.2 uses $D^3/(64d)$ and its proof uses $D/(2d)$. With Z-weight zero, its monomial set is not the intended finite interpolation space. Accordingly, the KTZ theorem is safe to cite here only for $1≤d<p$.\n\n[HKSS Theorem 4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.12752v1) assumes positive $d$ and $q>C d/ε^7$, and states a bivariate polynomial with $Ω(ε^4)$ agreement. This is historical context only. The arXiv record has only v1, dated 21 November 2023; its proof contains quantitative bookkeeping issues that should be resolved before its output exponent is reused.\n\nAt the final corpus audit, 2026-09-14 06:08:39 UTC, both campaigns had empty verified, promising, rejected, and bottleneck boards, and there were no completed responses or verifier audits. Four ten-agent jobs were running. Thus there was no prior mathematical submission to import. DATA_MANIFEST described the pre-run state and was stale during this live execution.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A — uniform occupancy obstruction (proved).** Let\n\n$$\nλ=log(4/e),\\qquad r_p=floor(log p/(4log log p)),\\qquad K_d=(d+1)(d+2)/2.\n$$\n\nFor every prime $p≥e^{16}$ and every $0≤d<p$ satisfying\n\n$$\nK_d log p≤λp/2,\n$$\n\nthere exist $f:F_p^2→F_p$ and a degree-at-most-$d$ line table such that\n\n$$\na≥r_p/(4p),\\qquad δ_d(f)≤2/p.\n$$\n\nHence $δ_d(f)/a≤8/r_p=o(1)$.\n\nIn particular:\n\n1. At $d=0$, the benchmark hypothesis $a≥C(d/p)^{1/3}$ is automatic, yet its linear global-agreement conclusion fails.\n2. Taking $d_p=floor(sqrt(r_p))$ gives $d_p→∞$, $a/(d_p/p)→∞$, and $δ_{d_p}/a→0$. Thus no absolute $C,c>0$ can make the bare implication $a≥C d/p⇒δ_d≥ca$ valid over the whole positive-degree range.\n3. For every fixed $η>0$, this construction has $a=o((d_p/p)^{1-η})$, so it does not refute the campaign's fixed-$η$ near-linear target.\n\n**Theorem B — degree-zero spectral repair (proved).** For every prime $p$, every point table, and every degree-zero line table,\n\n$$\nδ_0(f)≥a-1/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nConsequently, if $a≥2/sqrt(p+1)$ then some constant polynomial agrees with $f$ on at least $a/2$ of the plane.\n\n**Theorem C — incidence-only sparsification barrier (proved).** Let $p$ be prime, $1≤k≤p$, $d=k-1$, and $0<γ≤1$. There is a genuine degree-$d$ line-versus-point table with\n\n$$\na=ε_k=k/(p+1),\\qquad δ_d=k/p,\n$$\n\nwhose accepted graph is $k$-regular between all $p^2$ points and the $p^2$ finite-slope lines. If $k≥2$ and $R$ witnesses at least a $γ$ fraction of all accepted incidences—or at least $γk$ incidences on every accepted line—then\n\n$$\n|R|≥γp^2/(k-1)≥γp/ε_k.\n$$\n\nFor $k=1$, no accepted edge has an alternative accepted-line witness at all.\n\n## Proof\n\n**[P1, proved] Modal line labels reduce the local test to occupancy.** Choose $f$ uniformly from all functions $F_p^2→F_p$, independently at every point. On each line $L$, let $M_L$ be the largest multiplicity of a field value among the $p$ values of $f|_L$. For any fixed line, these are $p$ independent uniform colors, so $M_L$ has the law of the maximum load $M_p$ when $p$ balls are thrown into $p$ bins. No independence between different lines is needed. By linearity,\n\n$$\nE_L,E_f[M_L]=E[M_p].\n$$\n\nAfter $f$ is fixed, choose $P_L$ to be a modal value on $L$. These are constant polynomials and hence are legal for every $d≥0$. The resulting local agreement is $(E_L M_L)/p$.\n\n**[P2, proved] The modal load is logarithmically superconstant.** Let $N$ be Poisson with mean $p/2$ and expose one infinite sequence of independent uniform colors. Conditional on $N$, inspect the first $N$ colors. Poisson splitting makes the $p$ bin loads independent Poisson variables of mean $1/2$.\n\nPut $r=r_p$. Since $p≥e^{16}$, $r≥1$ and\n\n$$\nr log(2r)≤(log p)/4.\n$$\n\nFor $Y$ Poisson with mean $1/2$,\n\n$$\nPr[Y≥r]≥Pr[Y=r]=e^{-1/2}/(2^r r!)≥e^{-1/2}/(2r)^r≥e^{-1/2}p^{-1/4}.\n$$\n\nTherefore the probability that all $p$ Poissonized bin loads are below $r$ is at most\n\n$$\nexp(-e^{-1/2}p^{3/4}).\n$$\n\nThe Poisson Chernoff bound gives $Pr[N>p]≤(e/4)^{p/2}$. On $N≤p$, adding balls cannot decrease the maximum. Hence\n\n$$\nPr[M_p≥r]≥1-exp(-e^{-1/2}p^{3/4})-(e/4)^{p/2}≥1/2,\n$$\n\nand $E[M_p]≥r/2$.\n\n**[P3, proved] All degree-$d$ global polynomials can simultaneously have small agreement.** There are at most $p^{K_d}$ formal total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials. For any fixed $Q$, its number of agreements with random $f$ is binomial with parameters $p^2$ and $1/p$, hence mean $p$. The multiplicative Chernoff bound gives\n\n$$\nPr[|\\{x:Q(x)=f(x)\\}|≥2p]≤(e/4)^p=e^{-λp}.\n$$\n\nA union bound over all $Q$ gives bad probability\n\n$$\nβ≤exp(K_d log p-λp)≤e^{-λp/2}.\n$$\n\nThis is the only union bound over global polynomials.\n\n**[P4, proved] A deterministic table has both properties.** Let $Z=E_L M_L$, measured in points rather than normalized agreement. Then $0≤Z≤p$ and $E[Z]≥r/2$. On the event $G$ that every degree-$d$ polynomial has at most $2p$ agreements,\n\n$$\nE[Z1_G]≥r/2-pβ≥r/4\n$$\n\nfor $p≥e^{16}$. Thus some deterministic $f∈G$ has $Z≥r/4$. Label every line by a modal constant. This gives $a=Z/p≥r/(4p)$, while membership in $G$ gives $δ_d≤2/p$. This proves Theorem A. No Markov inequality and no union bound over affine lines is used.\n\n**[P5, proved] Consequences for the advertised thresholds.** When $d=0$, every positive power of $d/p$ is zero, while Theorem A has $δ_0/a≤8/r_p→0$. This refutes the workspace benchmark on its literal parameter range.\n\nFor the positive-degree consequence, set $d_p=floor(sqrt(r_p))$. Then $K_{d_p}log p=o(p)$, so Theorem A applies for all sufficiently large primes. Moreover,\n\n$$\na/(d_p/p)≥r_p/(4d_p)→∞,\n$$\n\nwhereas $δ_{d_p}/a≤8/r_p→0$. Given any proposed constants $C,c>0$, large enough $p$ therefore satisfies both $a≥Cd_p/p$ and $δ_{d_p}<ca$.\n\n**[P6, proved] Spectral repair at degree zero.** For each $z∈F_p$, let $X_z=\\{x:f(x)=z\\}$ and let $T_z=\\{L:P_L≡z\\}$. Write $u_z=|X_z|/p^2$ and $v_z=|T_z|/[p(p+1)]$. These are probability vectors. KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives\n\n$$\nPr[x∈X_z,L∈T_z]≤u_zv_z+sqrt(u_zv_z)/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nSumming over $z$,\n\n$$\na≤Σ_z u_zv_z+(1/sqrt(p+1))Σ_z sqrt(u_zv_z)\n  ≤max_z u_z+1/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nThe last step uses Cauchy–Schwarz exactly once: $Σ_z sqrt(u_zv_z)≤1$. Since $max_z u_z=δ_0$, Theorem B follows. There is no hidden Markov or union loss.\n\n**[P7, proved] Algebraic realization of the regular obstruction.** Fix $S⊆F_p$ of size $k$ and set $f(x,y)=x^k$. Parameterize finite-slope lines by\n\n$$\nL_{m,b}(t)=(t,mt+b).\n$$\n\nDefine\n\n$$\nP_{m,b}(t)=t^k-∏_{s∈S}(t+m-s).\n$$\n\nThe two displayed summands are monic of degree $k$, so their leading terms cancel and $deg P_{m,b}≤k-1=d$. On a vertical line $V_c(t)=(c,t)$, set $P_{V_c}(t)=c^k+1$, which never equals $f(c,t)=c^k$.\n\nOn a finite-slope line, $P_{m,b}(t)=f(L_{m,b}(t))$ exactly when $t+m∈S$. Thus every finite-slope line has exactly $k$ accepted points. At a point $(x,y)$, exactly the $k$ slopes $m∈S-x$ are accepted, while the vertical line is never accepted. The accepted graph between all points and finite-slope lines is therefore exactly $k$-regular. Its local agreement under the required all-line sampling is\n\n$$\na=kp^2/[p^2(p+1)]=k/(p+1).\n$$\n\n**[P8, proved] Witness counting forces $p/ε$ lines.** Let $C_R$ be the accepted incidences covered by another accepted line in $R$. Each selected finite-slope line contains $k$ accepted points; at each such point there are exactly $k-1$ other accepted lines. Hence the number of witness triples $(x,L,M)$ with $M∈R$, $L≠M$, and both incidences accepted is at most $|R|k(k-1)$. Multiple witnesses only overcount $C_R$, so\n\n$$\n|C_R|≤|R|k(k-1).\n$$\n\nCovering a $γ$ fraction of the $kp^2$ accepted incidences requires $|C_R|≥γkp^2$. Therefore\n\n$$\n|R|≥γp^2/(k-1)≥γp/ε_k,\n$$\n\nwhere the last inequality uses $k≤p$. Requiring this coverage on every line is stronger and gives the same bound. If selected-line edges were instead declared automatically covered, a modified count still yields $|R|=Ω(p/ε_k)$.\n\n**[P9, proved] The obstruction table itself remains globally sound.** For every total-degree-at-most-$(k-1)$ polynomial $Q$ and each fixed $y$, the formal polynomial $X^k-Q(X,y)$ has degree exactly $k$, so it has at most $k$ roots in $F_p$. Thus $δ_{k-1}≤k/p$. Equality is achieved by\n\n$$\nQ_S(X,Y)=X^k-∏_{s∈S}(X-s),\n$$\n\nwhose leading terms cancel and whose degree is at most $k-1$. Therefore $δ_{k-1}=k/p=(1+1/p)ε_k$. The example is not a soundness counterexample; it isolates the concentration architecture.\n\n**[P10, proved] The cubic bottleneck is reconstructed.** KTZ Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/ε)$. Weighted interpolation has $Θ(D^3/d)$ available monomials and $O(|R|D)$ constraints, so it selects\n\n$$\nD=Θ(sqrt(d|R|))=O(sqrt(dp/ε)).\n$$\n\nExtending the line identity and surviving the second pruning require $D<k_1/2$ with $k_1=Θ(εp)$. Hence\n\n$$\nsqrt(dp/ε)=O(εp)\\quad iff\\quad ε^3=Ω(d/p).\n$$\n\nTheorem C proves that the $p/ε$ input to this calculation cannot be improved using only the accepted graph and the same witness requirement. It does not rule out a hybrid lemma exploiting the actual polynomial labels.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Modal occupancy | $p$ balls, $p$ colors | probability factor $1/2$ | load $r_p/2$ |\n| Deterministic extraction | load $r_p/2$ | conditioning factor $1/2$ | $a≥r_p/(4p)$ |\n| Global code union | $p^{K_d}$ candidates | $e^{K_d log p}$ | $δ_d≤2/p$ if $K_d log p≤λp/2$ |\n| Linear conversion | $a≥r_p/(4p)$ | ratio $8/r_p$ | $δ_d=o(a)$ |\n| Exact exponent 1 | $d_p=sqrt(r_p)$ | $a/(d_p/p)→∞$ | bare $Cd/p$ threshold refuted |\n| Degree-zero repair | local $a$ | additive $1/sqrt(p+1)$ by Cauchy–Schwarz | $δ_0≥a-1/sqrt(p+1)$ |\n| KTZ sparsification | minimum degree $Θ(εp)$ | sampling probability $Θ(1/(εp))$ | $|R|=O(p/ε)$ |\n| New lower bound | regular accepted graph | witness capacity $k(k-1)$ per selected line | $|R|=Ω(p/ε)$ |\n| KTZ interpolation | $|R|=Θ(p/ε)$ | $D^3/d$ versus $|R|D$ | $D=Θ(sqrt(dp/ε))$ |\n| Root propagation | degree $D$ | require $D=O(εp)$ | $ε^3=Ω(d/p)$ |\n\nAll displayed exponent manipulations are included. No logarithm has been suppressed in a claimed power threshold.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Random modal-color table — successful.** This proves Theorem A and refutes the literal $d=0$ benchmark and a bare exact-linear threshold in a growing positive-degree regime.\n2. **Regular algebraic incidence table — successful as an architectural obstruction.** Theorem C matches the KTZ $p/ε$ selector size but has global agreement $(1+1/p)ε$, so it does not refute soundness.\n3. **Concentrated good directions — not worst case.** Taking $f=0$, setting $P_L=0$ on $s$ directions and $P_L=1$ elsewhere gives local agreement $s/(p+1)$. Its accepted graph can be covered at scale $Θ(p)$ rather than $Θ(p/ε)$; concentrated directions therefore do not explain the cubic bottleneck.\n4. **Small primes.** Exhaustive enumeration gives ratio $4/3$ at $p=2,d=0$ and $7/4$ at $p=3,d=0$. These do not prove divergence, but they reveal no exceptional collapse.\n5. **Near-maximal degree.** Theorem C permits $k=p,d=p-1$. Then $∏_{s∈F_p}(t-s)=t^p-t$ and all degree claims remain valid.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The probabilistic counterexample uses only iid values in $F_p$ and constant line polynomials. It has no separability assumption.\n- Theorem C uses distinct linear roots. At $k=p$, $t^p-t$ is squarefree because its derivative is $-1$. There is no hidden division by $k$, $d$, or a derivative.\n- No discriminant, resultant, irreducibility claim, Hasse derivative, or interpolation multiplicity appears in the new proofs.\n- KTZ's derivative and Newton-lifting machinery is not used to prove any new claim. Its division-by-$d$ monomial bound is precisely why its printed proof does not cover $d=0$.\n- The only Cauchy–Schwarz loss is the explicit $1/sqrt(p+1)$ term in [P6]. The only global union loss is $p^{K_d}$. No Markov inequality is used. Poisson and Chernoff losses are displayed in [P2]–[P4].\n- The line model is the full affine set, including vertical lines. Total degree is never replaced by individual degree. All auxiliary constructions obey $d<p$.\n- Finite computations were used solely for falsification; the asymptotic theorem is probabilistic but rigorous.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThis note proves no exponent greater than $1/3$ for $1≤d<p$. The occupancy construction lies below every fixed-$η$ threshold $(d/p)^{1-η}$ along the displayed growing-degree sequence, so the principal near-linear target remains open.\n\nThe degree-zero repair has a gap: the counterexample forces a floor of at least order $log p/(p log log p)$, while the spectral argument only proves linear recovery above order $p^{-1/2}$. The exact floor is undetermined.\n\nThe sparsifier lower bound applies to the KTZ witness definition, or any method based only on the accepted incidence graph. It does not preclude using polynomial coefficients, higher-order algebraic coincidences, or a simultaneous algebraic-concentration argument. Indeed, that is now the necessary next direction.\n\nFinally, the cited HKSS source is arXiv v1 and contains unresolved internal exponent bookkeeping. I prove sharp all-order lower bounds for point-centered and line-centered distinct-star moments of the accepted-incidence graph. The bounds are the adjacent-integer convex envelopes of falling factorials. I then give an explicit legal line-versus-point table at local agreement $\\epsilon_0=d/p$ whose accepted graph is connected, has full point and line support, and attains both families of moment bounds simultaneously for every admissible order. On the same table, every fractional family that reaches a $\\theta$ fraction of the accepted points of every line through other accepted lines has weight $\\Theta(\\theta p/\\epsilon_0)$, with exact bounds differing by at most $1.02$.\n\nEvery affine point-line incidence graph is $K_{2,2}$-free, so ordinary common-neighborhood dependent random choice on the raw accepted graph cannot produce a nontrivial biclique. I also prove an exact higher-moment DRC certificate for the auxiliary line-compatibility graph, including a concurrency correction that counts target lines receiving genuinely distinct intersection roots. Its acceptance-density-only specialization pays $\\epsilon^{2t}$ at moment order $t$; direct insertion into KTZ interpolation needs $t>256d$ and is therefore much worse than the cubic route.\n\nThese results isolate a proof-architecture barrier, not a soundness counterexample. The explicit extremizer has $f=0$, and the single total-degree-zero polynomial $Q=0$ agrees globally everywhere. Accordingly, the unconditional exponent-$1/3$ benchmark is not improved.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nLet $\\mathcal L$ be the $p(p+1)$ affine lines of $\\mathbb F_p^2$. Each line contains $p$ points and each point lies on $p+1$ lines. A valid table consists of\n\n$$\nf:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p,\n\\qquad\nP_L\\in\\mathbb F_p[t],\\quad \\deg P_L\\le d\\quad(L\\in\\mathcal L),\n$$\n\nusing a fixed affine parameterization of each line. Put\n\n$$\nE=\\{(x,L):x\\in L,\\ P_L(x)=f(x)\\},\n\\qquad\n\\epsilon=\\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}.\n$$\n\nThis is exactly uniform affine-line sampling followed by a uniform point of the line. Because the incidence graph is biregular, it is equivalently a uniform point followed by a uniform incident line. Define accepted degrees\n\n$$\na_x=|\\{L\\ni x:(x,L)\\in E\\}|,\n\\qquad\nb_L=|\\{x\\in L:(x,L)\\in E\\}|.\n$$\n\nFor integers $u,s\\ge0$, let $(u)_s=u(u-1)\\cdots(u-s+1)$, with $(u)_0=1$. For $\\mu\\in[0,n]$, write $k=\\lfloor\\mu\\rfloor$ and $\\rho=\\mu-k$, and define the adjacent-integer interpolation\n\n$$\nJ_s(\\mu)=(1-\\rho)(k)_s+\\rho(k+1)_s.\n$$\n\nFor $0\\le s\\le p+1$, let $\\Gamma_s^P$ be the probability that, after choosing uniform $x$, an ordered $s$-tuple of distinct lines through $x$ consists entirely of accepted incidences. For $0\\le s\\le p$, define $\\Gamma_s^L$ analogously by choosing a uniform line and an ordered $s$-tuple of distinct points on it. Tildes, as in $\\widetilde\\Gamma_s^P$, denote independent sampling with replacement.\n\nFor fractional reaching, let $\\lambda_M\\ge0$ be line weights and set\n\n$$\nu_{x,L}(\\lambda)=\n\\min\\left\\{1,\n\\sum_{\\substack{M\\ni x,\\ M\\ne L\\\\(x,M)\\in E}}\\lambda_M\n\\right\\}.\n$$\n\nThe weights are $\\theta$-reaching if\n\n$$\n\\sum_{x:(x,L)\\in E}u_{x,L}(\\lambda)\\ge\\theta b_L\n$$\n\nfor every line $L$, where $0<\\theta\\le1$. Let $\\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta$ be the minimum of $\\sum_M\\lambda_M$.\n\nFinally, the auxiliary compatibility graph $H$ has vertex set $\\mathcal L$. Distinct lines are adjacent when they are nonparallel and both accept at their unique intersection.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe benchmark is [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, Revision 1, Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, acceptance $\\epsilon\\ge C(d/q)^{1/3}$ yields one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with global agreement at least $c\\epsilon$. Only its $m=2$, $q=p$ specialization is used here.\n\nThe following exponent explanation is my reconstruction, not a quoted KTZ theorem. KTZ Lemma 3.2 selects $|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)$ lines. Lemmas 2.2 and 4.1--4.2 give a weighted-degree explainer\n\n$$\nD=O\\!\\left(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon}\\right).\n$$\n\nLemma 4.3 and the lifting step require $D=O(\\epsilon p)$. Hence\n\n$$\n\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon}=O(\\epsilon p)\n\\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p).\n$$\n\nThe active verifier board accepts two earlier results. Researcher-0002 proves a component-sensitive decoder and a conditional exponent $1/2$ when a pruned component has line measure $O(\\epsilon)$. Researcher-0006 isolates singular lifted incidences as an algebraic obstruction. Researchers 0001, 0004, 0005, 0007, and 0008 are revise-grade; researcher-0003's exact aggregate theorem was rejected for omitted interpolation hypotheses. In particular, researcher-0004 proves uniform interpolation multiplicity exponent-neutral, while researcher-0008 proves the exact second collision identity and a nearly regular carrier. The present note independently re-proves and strengthens the latter to every moment order, gives a simpler explicit carrier, and proves that its accepted graph is connected. The live leaderboards, rather than the launch-time data manifest, determine these statuses.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem 1 (sharp raw moments and a connected simultaneous extremizer).** Fix a prime $p$ and $101\\le d<p$.\n\n1. For every valid table of agreement $\\epsilon$,\n\n$$\n\\Gamma_s^P=\n\\frac{\\mathbb E_x[(a_x)_s]}{(p+1)_s}\n\\ge\n\\frac{J_s((p+1)\\epsilon)}{(p+1)_s}\n\\qquad(0\\le s\\le p+1),\n$$\n\nand\n\n$$\n\\Gamma_s^L=\n\\frac{\\mathbb E_L[(b_L)_s]}{(p)_s}\n\\ge\n\\frac{J_s(p\\epsilon)}{(p)_s}\n\\qquad(0\\le s\\le p).\n$$\n\nFor every integer $r\\ge1$,\n\n$$\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_r^P\\ge\\epsilon^r,\n\\qquad\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_r^L\\ge\\epsilon^r.\n$$\n\n2. There is an explicit legal table with $\\epsilon_0=d/p$ such that its accepted graph is connected,\n\n$$\nb_L=d\\quad\\text{for every }L,\n$$\n\nand\n\n$$\na_x=\n\\begin{cases}\nd+1,&\\text{at exactly }pd\\text{ points},\\\\\nd,&\\text{at exactly }p(p-d)\\text{ points}.\n\\end{cases}\n$$\n\nIt simultaneously attains both distinct-star lower envelopes for every admissible $s$:\n\n$$\n\\Gamma_s^P=\n\\frac{(1-d/p)(d)_s+(d/p)(d+1)_s}{(p+1)_s},\n\\qquad\n\\Gamma_s^L=\\frac{(d)_s}{(p)_s}.\n$$\n\nIts line-centered with-replacement moments equal $\\epsilon_0^r$ for every $r\\ge1$.\n\n3. On this table, for every $0<\\theta\\le1$,\n\n$$\n\\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d+1}\n\\le\\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta\n\\le\n\\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d-1}.\n$$\n\n4. Every accepted affine point-line graph is $K_{2,2}$-free. Thus two or more distinct vertices sampled from either shore have at most one common neighbor on the other shore.\n\nThe constructed table has $f=0$, and $Q=0$ has global agreement one.\n\n**Theorem 2 (auxiliary compatibility-graph DRC with concurrency correction).** For any valid table, let $N=p(p+1)$, $\\mu=(p+1)\\epsilon$, and let $\\bar\\Delta$ be the average degree of $H$. Then\n\n$$\ne(H)=\\sum_x\\binom{a_x}{2},\n\\qquad\n\\bar\\Delta\\ge\\frac{p\\mu(\\mu-1)}{p+1}.\n$$\n\nFor every integer $1\\le t\\le\\lfloor\\bar\\Delta\\rfloor$, define\n\n$$\nM_t(H)=\n\\frac{\\sum_{L\\in\\mathcal L}\\binom{\\deg_H(L)}t}{\\binom Nt}.\n$$\n\nThere is a set $S$ of $t$ distinct seed lines with at least $M_t(H)$ common neighbors. If $1\\le h\\le t$ and $h_L$ is the number of distinct points among $\\{L\\cap M:M\\in S\\}$, then the same $S$ has at least\n\n$$\nM_t(H)-\n\\frac{\\binom t2(p+1)}{t-h+1}\n$$\n\ncommon-neighbor lines satisfying $h_L\\ge h$. Moreover,\n\n$$\nM_t(H)\\ge\nN\\frac{\\binom{\\lfloor\\bar\\Delta\\rfloor}t}{\\binom Nt}.\n$$\n\nIf $\\mu\\ge2$ and $\\bar\\Delta\\ge2t+2$, the last expression is at least $N(\\epsilon^2/4)^t$.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n### [P1] — proved: exact star identities\n\nDouble counting accepted incidences gives\n\n$$\n\\mathbb E_x a_x=(p+1)\\epsilon,\n\\qquad\n\\mathbb E_L b_L=p\\epsilon.\n$$\n\nAt a fixed point $x$, precisely $(a_x)_s$ ordered tuples of $s$ distinct incident lines are wholly accepted, out of $(p+1)_s$. Averaging proves the point identity. The line identity is identical with $b_L$ and $(p)_s$. No independence or concentration estimate is used.\n\n### [P2] — proved: sharp discrete moment lower envelope\n\nFor $F_s(j)=(j)_s$ on nonnegative integers,\n\n$$\n\\Delta F_s(j)=s(j)_{s-1},\n\\qquad\n\\Delta^2F_s(j)=s(s-1)(j)_{s-2}\\ge0.\n$$\n\nThus the piecewise-linear interpolation of $F_s$ is convex. Jensen gives\n\n$$\n\\mathbb E[(A)_s]\\ge J_s(\\mathbb EA)\n$$\n\nfor every integer-valued degree variable $A$. The minimizer need not be unique when the falling factorial vanishes, but the adjacent-integer mixture always attains the minimum. Applying this to [P1] proves the distinct-star inequalities.\n\nFor sampling with replacement,\n\n$$\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_r^P=\n\\mathbb E_x\\left(\\frac{a_x}{p+1}\\right)^r,\n\\qquad\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_r^L=\n\\mathbb E_L\\left(\\frac{b_L}{p}\\right)^r.\n$$\n\nOrdinary Jensen for $z\\mapsto z^r$ gives the two $\\epsilon^r$ bounds. Repeated samples must not be confused with distinct constraints: $a^r=\\sum_j {r\\brace j}(a)_j$ includes duplicate-line events.\n\n### [P3] — proved: explicit legal carrier\n\nLet\n\n$$\nS_d=\\{0,1,\\ldots,d-1\\}\\subset\\mathbb F_p\n$$\n\nand set $f(x,y)=0$. For a nonvertical line\n\n$$\nL_{m,b}(t)=(t,mt+b),\n$$\n\nset\n\n$$\nP_{m,b}(t)=\\prod_{s\\in S_d}(t+m-s).\n$$\n\nFor the vertical line $V_c(t)=(c,t)$, set\n\n$$\nP_{V_c}(t)=\\prod_{s\\in S_d}(t-s).\n$$\n\nAll labels have formal degree exactly $d<p$. A nonvertical incidence at $(x,y)$ accepts exactly when $x+m\\in S_d$. Therefore every point has exactly $d$ accepted nonvertical lines, one for each slope $m=s-x$, $s\\in S_d$. Its vertical line also accepts exactly when $y\\in S_d$. Hence the asserted point degrees hold. Every nonvertical line has the $d$ roots $t=s-m$, and every vertical line has the $d$ roots $t=s$. Thus every line degree is $d$.\n\nThere are $dp(p+1)$ accepted incidences, so\n\n$$\n\\epsilon_0=\n\\frac{dp(p+1)}{p^2(p+1)}=\frac dp.\n$$\n\n### [P4] — proved: connectivity\n\nBecause $d\\ge101$, the elements $0,1,2$ belong to $S_d$. For any $(x,y)$, put\n\n$$\nC=(x-1,y+x-1).\n$$\n\nThe points $(x,y)$ and $C$ lie on a line of slope $1-x$ and have acceptance values $x+(1-x)=1$ and $(x-1)+(1-x)=0$. The points $C$ and $(x,y+1)$ lie on a line of slope $2-x$ and have acceptance values $1$ and $2$. Thus $(x,y)$ and $(x,y+1)$ are joined by a four-edge accepted path.\n\nAlso, $(x,y)$ and $(x+1,y-x)$ share the accepted line of slope $-x$, since their acceptance values are $0$ and $1$. Vertical unit moves connect every point in a fixed column; the second move connects column $x$ to column $x+1$. Since $1$ generates the additive group of the prime field, every point vertex lies in one component. Every line vertex has $d>0$ accepted neighbors, so the full accepted bipartite graph is connected.\n\n### [P5] — proved: simultaneous moment extremality\n\nFor the carrier,\n\n$$\n(p+1)\\epsilon_0=d+d/p.\n$$\n\nThe point-degree distribution is exactly the adjacent mixture at this mean: degree $d+1$ has probability $d/p=\\epsilon_0$, and degree $d$ has probability $1-\\epsilon_0$. The line mean is $p\\epsilon_0=d$, and every line has that degree. Equality therefore holds in both inequalities of [P2] for every admissible $s$.\n\nIn particular, $\\Gamma_s^L=0$ for $s>d$ and $\\Gamma_s^P=0$ for $s>d+1$. Fixed mean alone cannot manufacture more distinct algebraic constraints than the local degree permits. At $s=2$,\n\n$$\n\\Gamma_2^P=\n\\epsilon_0^2-\n\\frac{\\epsilon_0(1-\\epsilon_0)}{p+1}.\n$$\n\nFor $2\\le s\\le(d+1)/2$,\n\n$$\n2^{-(s-1)}\\epsilon_0^s\n\\le\\frac{(d)_s}{(p)_s}\n\\le\\epsilon_0^s.\n$$\n\nThe exact product, rather than this coarse comparison, is retained in the theorem.\n\n### [P6] — proved: fractional other-line reaching\n\nWeights may be truncated to $[0,1]$ without changing capped loads; compactness therefore makes the minimum attainable. Put\n\n$$\nv_x=\n\\min\\left\\{1,\n\\sum_{M\\ni x:(x,M)\\in E}\\lambda_M\n\\right\\}.\n$$\n\nSince $u_{x,L}\\le v_x$, any $\\theta$-reaching weights satisfy\n\n$$\n\\theta d\\,p(p+1)\n\\le\\sum_x a_xv_x\n\\le(d+1)\\sum_xv_x\n\\le d(d+1)\\sum_M\\lambda_M.\n$$\n\nThis proves the lower bound. Conversely, assign every line weight $\\theta/(d-1)$. At an accepted incidence, at least $a_x-1\\ge d-1$ other accepted lines occur, so $u_{x,L}\\ge\\theta$. This proves the upper bound. Their ratio is\n\n$$\n\\frac{d+1}{d-1}\\le\\frac{102}{100}.\n$$\n\nSince $d=p\\epsilon_0$, the cost is $\\Theta(\\theta p/\\epsilon_0)$ with explicit constants.\n\n### [P7] — proved: raw DRC collapse\n\nTwo distinct affine points determine one affine line, and two distinct affine lines meet in at most one point. Hence the full affine incidence graph, and every accepted subgraph, contains no $K_{2,2}$. A common-neighborhood DRC sample containing at least two distinct raw vertices therefore has common neighborhood of size at most one. If sampling with replacement appears to give a large common neighborhood, after deduplication it is either a one-vertex star or has common neighborhood at most one.\n\nThis assertion concerns only the raw point-line graph. Auxiliary compatibility graphs may contain many four-cycles.\n\n### [P8] — proved: auxiliary edge count\n\nEvery unordered pair of accepted lines through $x$ gives one edge of $H$, and every edge has a unique intersection point. Therefore\n\n$$\ne(H)=\\sum_x\\binom{a_x}{2}.\n$$\n\nSince $N=p(p+1)$,\n\n$$\n\\bar\\Delta=\n\\frac{2e(H)}N\n=\frac{p\\,\\mathbb E_x[a_x(a_x-1)]}{p+1}\n\\ge\\frac{p\\mu(\\mu-1)}{p+1},\n$$\n\nwhere the last step is convexity. The sharper adjacent-integer form follows by replacing $\\mu(\\mu-1)$ with $J_2(\\mu)$.\n\n### [P9] — proved: exact auxiliary DRC moment\n\nCount pairs $(S,L)$ in which $S$ is a $t$-element subset of $N_H(L)$. Their number is\n\n$$\n\\sum_L\\binom{\\deg_H(L)}t.\n$$\n\nAveraging over the $\\binom Nt$ choices of $S$ gives a seed set with at least $M_t(H)$ common neighbors. Discrete convexity of $j\\mapsto\\binom jt$ gives\n\n$$\nM_t(H)\\ge\nN\\frac{\\binom{\\lfloor\\bar\\Delta\\rfloor}t}{\\binom Nt}.\n$$\n\nIf $\\bar\\Delta\\ge2t+2$, every numerator factor is at least $\\bar\\Delta/2$, so the ratio is at least $(\\bar\\Delta/(2N))^t$. By [P8] and $\\mu\\ge2$,\n\n$$\n\\frac{\\bar\\Delta}{2N}\n\\ge\n\\frac{\\mu(\\mu-1)}{2(p+1)^2}\n\\ge\\frac{\\epsilon^2}{4}.\n$$\n\nThis proves the simplified bound.\n\n### [P10] — proved: concurrency correction\n\nFix the seed set from [P9]. For a common neighbor $L$, partition the $t$ seed lines according to their intersection point with $L$. If fewer than $h$ distinct points occur, the partition creates at least $t-h+1$ colliding seed pairs. A fixed pair of seed lines can collide on at most the $p+1$ lines through their own intersection; a parallel pair contributes none. Double counting bad targets and colliding seed pairs gives\n\n$$\n|\\{L\\in N_H(S):h_L<h\\}|\n\\le\n\\frac{\\binom t2(p+1)}{t-h+1}.\n$$\n\nSubtracting this from the common-neighbor count proves Theorem 2. If an explainer vanishes identically on every seed graph, each of the $h_L$ distinct intersections is a distinct root on the target graph, so the correction measures the root supply relevant to interpolation.\n\n### [P11] — proved: direct DRC insertion is quantitatively insufficient\n\nIn the KTZ coefficient-count construction, interpolating $t$ seed graphs uses\n\n$$\nD_t=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{dt}\\rfloor+1).\n$$\n\nEven before cleanup, transfer to a common-neighbor target needs $h_L>D_t$. Since $h_L\\le t$, this forces\n\n$$\nt>D_t>16\\sqrt{dt},\n\\qquad\\text{hence}\\qquad t>256d.\n$$\n\nReplacing the exact auxiliary moment $M_t(H)$ by the guarantee obtainable from acceptance density alone gives $N(\\epsilon^2/4)^t$. At the benchmark scale $\\epsilon=C(d/p)^{1/3}$, for fixed admissible $d$ and fixed $t>256d$,\n\n$$\nN(\\epsilon^2/4)^t\n=O_{C,d,t}(p^{2-2t/3})\n\\longrightarrow0.\n$$\n\nThus this black-box all-common-neighbor DRC certificate does not even guarantee one target line in the lower-boundary asymptotic regime. This does not rule out exploiting larger observed moments, label classes, or special structure in $H$.\n\n### [P12] — proved: scope of the obstruction\n\nThe carrier from [P3]--[P6] is connected, uses every line, attains all degree-distribution moment minima, and has essentially maximal universal reaching cost, yet $Q=0$ decodes it perfectly. Consequently, a valid stronger soundness proof may not treat moment regularity, broad support, connectivity, or large reaching cost alone as evidence of hardness. It must branch on polynomial-label or value coherence. This is a precise incidence-only obstruction, not a claim that every auxiliary or label-aware DRC argument fails.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output/status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Degree means | $\\epsilon$ | none | $(p+1)\\epsilon$ and $p\\epsilon$; proved |\n| Repeated $s$-moment | $\\epsilon$ | $s$th power | at least $\\epsilon^s$; sharp; proved |\n| Distinct $s$-moment | mean degree | exact falling-factorial correction | $J_s(\\mu)/(n)_s$; sharp; proved |\n| Compatibility graph | $\\epsilon$ | two acceptances | density scale $\\epsilon^2$; proved |\n| Auxiliary DRC | compatibility density | $t$th power | density-only certificate $N(\\epsilon^2/4)^t$; proved under stated hypotheses |\n| Direct root supply | $D_t=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{dt}\\rfloor+1)$ | $h\\le t$ | requires $t>256d$; proved |\n| Cubic-scale DRC substitution | $\\epsilon=C(d/p)^{1/3}$ | $\\epsilon^{2t}$ | $O(p^{2-2t/3})\\to0$ for fixed $t>256d$; proved |\n| Fractional reaching | $\\epsilon_0=d/p$ | one inverse $\\epsilon_0$ | $\\Theta(\\theta p/\\epsilon_0)$; proved |\n| KTZ selector | $\\epsilon$ | $\\epsilon^{-1}$ | $|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)$; quoted |\n| KTZ interpolation | $|R|$ | square root | $D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})$; reconstructed |\n| KTZ transfer | $D=O(\\epsilon p)$ | cubic comparison | $\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)$; reconstructed |\n| Constructed decoder | $f=0$ | none | global agreement $1$; proved |\n\nNo logarithmic, Markov, union, or Cauchy--Schwarz loss is hidden in the new results.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\nThe connected carrier is a successful counterexample to any universal claim that higher degree moments, connectivity, full support, or fractional relaxation automatically produce an $o(p/\\epsilon)$ reaching family. It is not a soundness counterexample: the labels visibly share $Q=0$.\n\nConcentrated good directions give a complementary stress test. Choose $k$ projective directions, put $f=0$, label their lines by zero and every other line by one. Every point has accepted degree $k$, so all point-centered with-replacement moments equal $\\epsilon^s$ exactly for $\\epsilon=k/(p+1)$. However, the auxiliary compatibility graph between two accepted parallel classes contains a $K_{p,p}$. Thus raw-graph $K_{2,2}$-freeness cannot be asserted for $H$.\n\nThe prior modal construction at ambient $d=101$ genuinely refutes a uniform exact-linear trigger $C d/p$ with global recovery $c\\epsilon$, but its local agreement is $\\Theta(\\log p/(p\\log\\log p))$, below every fixed $(101/p)^{1-\\eta}$ trigger. It does not obstruct the long-term target.\n\nA random point table with linewise interpolation guarantees roughly $d/p$ local agreement and can rule out exponents above one in suitable regimes. It does not yield a uniform fixed-$\\eta$ counterexample, especially when $d$ approaches $p$, and is not used in the theorem.\n\nNo inseparable construction affects the proof: $d<p$ prevents $t^p-t$ aliases. At $d=p-1$ the carrier remains valid and connected. At the lower boundary $d=101$, the first possible prime $p=103$ satisfies all denominators and root counts.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The field is exactly $\\mathbb F_p$ and $101\\le d<p$ throughout.\n- The set $S_d$ consists of distinct field elements. Each line label is a product of $d$ distinct linear factors and has exactly $d$ roots.\n- No derivative, Hasse derivative, discriminant, resultant, irreducibility, or absolute irreducibility input is used.\n- No field division by a derivative or slope occurs. Vertical lines are handled by their own parameterization.\n- The fractional division by $d-1$ is over the real weight space and is valid because $d\\ge101$.\n- The global polynomial $Q=0$ is a total-degree-at-most-$d$ decoder in an ambient test with $d>100$; no excluded degree parameter is analyzed.\n- The new proof has no Markov, union-bound, or Cauchy--Schwarz step. Discrete and ordinary Jensen losses are displayed exactly.\n- KTZ's Chernoff/union/Chebyshev selector losses belong only to the cited comparison and do not change its power of $\\epsilon$.\n- Finite computations were used only to check formulas, never to prove the asymptotic statements.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe benchmark is not improved, and no new global soundness theorem is claimed. The explicit carrier lies at $\\epsilon_0=d/p$, below every fixed $(d/p)^{1-\\eta}$ trigger because $0<d/p<1$, and it has a perfect decoder.\n\nThe $K_{2,2}$ obstruction applies only to the raw point-line incidence graph. Auxiliary compatibility graphs, factor graphs, and lifted incidence graphs may contain large bicliques. Theorem 2 is therefore a usable diagnostic rather than an impossibility theorem for all DRC variants.\n\nThe density-only lower bound for $M_t(H)$ can be far from the actual higher moment. A successful proof could exploit unusually large compatibility moments, provided it also controls concurrency and singular lifted roots. Conversely, the present note gives no realizable pseudorandom example proving that the auxiliary bound is sharp.\n\nFinally, moment and cover data discard polynomial labels. A line-polynomial graph is\n\\(\\Gamma_L=\\{(L(t),p_L(t)):t\\in\\mathbb F_p\\}\\).\n\nThe case \\(d=0\\) is treated separately because the above weight gives \\(Z\\) weight zero and the unrestricted weighted interpolation space is infinite-dimensional.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe controlling source is [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download). Their exact bivariate parameters are\n\\[\n100p\\le |\\mathcal R|\\le \\frac{6400p}{\\epsilon},\\qquad\nD=16\\bigl(\\lfloor\\sqrt{d|\\mathcal R|}\\rfloor+1\\bigr),\\qquad\nk_1=\\lfloor\\epsilon p/1000\\rfloor.\n\\]\nLemma 2.2 supplies \\(|V_D|\\ge D^3/(64d)\\); Lemmas 4.1--4.3 compare this with \\(|\\mathcal R|(D+1)\\) constraints and require \\(D<k_1/2\\).
